detail.abstract: Swarm intelligence changes the unit at which capability and failure must be evaluated. A collective can combine partial observations, distribute work and preserve useful activity after local loss; the same interactions can also correlate errors, conceal shared constraints and sustain action after an apparent stop. Twenty new infrastructure illustrations connect electricity, communication, logistics, invoices and accountability to service continuity and recovery. Ten worked cases, accompanied by twenty further illustrations, explain who can be affected, how a collective failure unfolds and which claims are supported by evidence available in 2026. A comparative analysis distinguishes water, fish, birds, bees, ants and software agents without treating them as one mechanism. This paper examines those mechanisms through a critical review of biological, computational, robotic and software-agent evidence, interpreted through the Architecture of Freedom Intelligence (AFI). AFI distinguishes actually available paths from represented paths and asks whether intelligent action reveals, creates and preserves useful continuations. Its fifth thesis, Freedom Intelligence, provides the organizing design question: whose practical options improve when a collective becomes more capable? The paper separates documented incidents from controlled demonstrations and hypothetical applications. Six reproducible numerical studies isolate evidence dependence, amplification, capacity admission, synchronized correction, revocation and falsepath filtering. A separate geometric laboratory illustrates eight movement conditions and a matched obstacle-protection intervention. These studies demonstrate consequences of specified rules, not incident frequencies or general empirical validation of AFI. The resulting architecture connects perception, memory, delegation and execution to independent constraints, recovery and human agency. Sixty scenario protocols and forty-eight capability specifications extend the analysis within the same document. The central conclusion is conditional: distributed intelligence becomes a systemic concern when interactiondependent behavior acquires consequential authority across shared dependencies; agent count or coherent appearance alone is insufficient.

detail.abstract: Equality, diversity, and inclusion (EDI) constitute essential pillars for sustainable innovation in the Nigerian higher education system. Accordingly, this study investigated the lived experiences of Office Technology and Management (OTM) teaching staff undertaking doctoral studies at a private university in Ibadan, Nigeria, through a qualitative research approach involving in-depth interviews and thematic analysis. A purposive sampling strategy was employed to recruit Office Technology and Management (OTM) teaching staff from polytechnics who were undertaking their PhD programmes at a private university. Four overarching themes emerged from the findings: previous experience syndrome, professional striving, organisational barriers, and personal barriers. The findings revealed that prioritising inclusivity enables institutions to empower PhD students to develop sustainable and innovative approaches to managing information and office environments. Accordingly, the study recommends that academic institutions invest in research capacity development and provide targeted mentorship programmes, both of which are critical for promoting sustainability.

detail.abstract: Humanity it seems is sleepwalking toward collapse as the Planet Earth entity is currently facing a metacrisis. Climate change, AI acceleration, geopolitical fragmentation, institutional erosion, and global governance failure are not separate crises or a polycrisis, but are a single, interconnected multi-dimensional metacrisis. Unfortunately, our existing governance systems were not designed to cope with such a challenge. In such circumstances, the survival of humanity and the preservation of our Planet Earth system must be viewed as our primary global strategic objective. This is not a choice, it is an imperative, and a calling for each of us to become the global guardians of our future. This paper provides a guide and a comprehensive framework for human survival - uniting governance reform, value management, distributed guardianship, and multi-domain defense under the Human Preservation Imperative (HPI). The paper suggests that the preservation of our species and the survival of human civilization has become the most important project in human history.

detail.abstract: Food logistics security is often managed through separate investments in physical controls, cybersecurity, information governance, supplier assurance, cold-chain monitoring, and continuity preparedness. This paper treats these controls as a portfolio whose business value depends on expected loss, tail risk, and service continuity. A reproducible Monte Carlo design generated 1,200 feasible security allocations subject to a fixed budget. Each portfolio was evaluated against synthetic theft, tampering, cyber, information-integrity, supplier, cold-chain, and disruption risks. Expected loss ranged from 22.64 to 37.96 index points, while conditional value at risk at the 95th percentile ranged from 132.86 to 222.46. The selected compromise portfolio allocated 12.6% to physical security, 22.0% to cybersecurity, 20.4% to information governance, 13.3% to supplier assurance, 14.5% to cold-chain monitoring, and 17.2% to continuity preparedness. It achieved expected loss of 22.77, CVaR95 of 132.86, and service continuity of 84.74. Only two portfolios lay on the strict efficient frontier, showing that small allocation changes can alter the balance between average loss, extreme loss, and continuity. The analysis demonstrates a transparent risk-return method; it does not estimate actual Egyptian firms or incidents. AI use disclosure. Generative AI tools assisted with language drafting, document formatting, and programming support. Farouk Eldakhlawy is responsible for independently verifying the research design, assumptions, code, numerical outputs, citations, figures, interpretations, and final text and for approving any version submitted or publicly posted.

detail.abstract: Radio spectrum governance is shifting from periodic administrative assignment to continuous and partly automated authorisation, which turns the speed and transparency of regulatory decisions into performance variables. This scoping review maps how the literature conceptualises regulatory agility and structures the multi-criteria trade-offs spectrum decisions require. Following Joanna Briggs Institute methodology and reporting under PRISMA-ScR, we searched Scopus for Englishlanguage studies published between 2015 and 2026, screened 267 records against staged eligibility criteria using three reviewer roles, and charted 20 included studies against 36 items. Every study identified decision criteria, yet only four elicited weights and only one defined the agility construct it invoked. Extraction produced 189 verbatim criterion statements, consolidated into 44 criteria across six dimensions, dominated by technical criteria with sustainability represented by only four occurrences. Seven studies located agility in regulatory instruments rather than organisational capability, eight treated incumbent protection as a hard constraint rather than a weighted criterion, and six responded to institutional slowness by moving decisions into automated systems. Weights are therefore not absent from spectrum governance but unstated, migrating into protection margins and priority-scoring code where they are least contestable. Making preference structures explicit is a precondition for accountable automated allocation.

detail.abstract: Modeling the joint distribution of extreme values in high-dimensional financial time series is challenging because extremes are sparse and locally extreme observations are not necessarily extreme relative to their full marginal distribution. To address this, we introduce a time-dependent network Hüsler-Reiss model in which market-informed adjacency matrices determine how strongly observations contribute to the estimation. We propose binary and weighted specifications, including the Joint Extremes Adjacency Matrix (JEAM) which combines information about individual extremeness with historical patterns of joint extreme movements. In the forecasting evaluation part, covering one-minute stock returns from three sectors of the S&P 100, JEAM achieves the best out-of-sample log scores for both tail directions; improving scores by 12.5-13.6% in the lower tail and 11.4-14.9% in the upper tail. The results show that incorporating market-informed network structures in the estimation, improves forecast evaluation of extremes across time series.

detail.abstract: Conditional grants play a critical role in supporting the development and sustainability of local government and infrastructure provision in South Africa. However, over time, evidence has shown that municipalities are plagued by administrative inefficiencies that lead to under-expenditure and grant forfeitures, thereby negatively impacting service delivery. This paper adopted a qualitative research approach to examine the impact of conditional grant under-expenditure on municipal service delivery and sustainable local government in South Africa. The paper relied on secondary data from academic literature, government reports, Auditor-General findings, and policy documents. The findings revealed that weak administrative capacity, poor financial management, ineffective planning, governance deficiencies, and delays in project implementation contributed to the under-utilization of conditional grants, delaying the delivery of essential services such as water, sanitation, housing, roads, and electricity, thereby undermining social and environmental sustainability. The paper concluded that conditional grant under-expenditure is not merely a financial management problem, but a systemic governance and institutional challenge that undermines sustainable local government and developmental service delivery in South Africa. The study further recommends adopting an Integrated Municipal Conditional Grant Management Model to strengthen institutional capacity, governance accountability, expenditure performance, and intergovernmental coordination within municipalities.

title: Investigating the Effect of Channel Sparsity on the Performance of Beamspace Estimation Algorithms in 5G mmWave Massive MIMO

detail.title: Investigating the Effect of Channel Sparsity on the Performance of Beamspace Estimation Algorithms in 5G mmWave Massive MIMO

detail.abstract: Millimeter-wave (mmWave) massive multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) systems constitute a cornerstone technology for fifth-generation (5G) wireless networks, enabling unprecedented data rates through the utilization of abundant high-frequency spectrum. Beamspace channel estimation has emerged as a transformative approach to address the formidable pilot overhead and computational complexity challenges inherent in large-scale antenna arrays, leveraging the inherent sparsity of mmWave propagation channels. This sparsity, however, is not immutable and is subject to degradation arising from real-world propagation phenomena including dense scattering environments, user mobility, and hardware non-idealities such as power leakage in lens antenna arrays. This paper presents a comprehensive investigation into the effect of varying channel sparsity levels on the estimation accuracy and spectral efficiency of prominent beamspace channel estimation algorithms for 5G mmWave massive MIMO systems. Employing a 3D metallic plate lens antenna architecture as the beamspace transformation mechanism, we systematically evaluate the performance of classical Compressive Sensing (CS) algorithms-specifically Orthogonal Matching Pursuit (OMP) and its variants-across a spectrum of sparsity ratios, ranging from highly sparse lineof-sight conditions to increasingly dense urban micro-cell scenarios. Our analysis incorporates a realistic 5G MIMO-OFDM statistical channel model to capture the multipath characteristics of mmWave propagation. Extensive simulation results reveal a critical performance threshold: beamspace estimation algorithms exhibit graceful degradation when sparsity levels remain below 25%, yet experience catastrophic failure and convergence instability when sparsity ratios exceed approximately 40%, effectively eroding the spectral efficiency gains promised by massive MIMO. Furthermore, we quantify the synergistic detrimental impact of power leakage-an inherent artifact of practical 3D lens antennas-which artificially reduces effective sparsity by inducing energy spread across adjacent beams. The findings establish a quantitative benchmark for the maximum permissible channel densification before beamspace processing becomes counterproductive, providing essential design guidelines for adaptive hybrid beamforming architectures in next-generation wireless systems. This work underscores that while beamspace channel estimation remains a powerful enabler for 5G mmWave communications, its practical efficacy is intrinsically bounded by environmental and hardwareinduced sparsity constraints, necessitating robust algorithmic innovations for future deployments in increasingly complex propagation environments.

detail.abstract: Between 2025 and 2027 Korea enacted its widest revision of corporate governance law in decades: a one-third independent-director floor in place of one quarter, an aggregated 3% voting cap at audit-committee elections, separate election of two audit committee members, mandatory cumulative voting at large firms, an expanded directors' fiduciary duty, electronic general meetings, and mandatory cancellation of treasury shares. The reform lands unevenly, and public disclosure does not let a shareholder tell which holdings must change. We conduct a firm-level ex-ante impact assessment across a near-census of 2,637 currently listed non-SPV firms -- 95.6% of the 2,759 firms listed on the Korea Exchange -- and build from public disclosure a reproducible taxonomy assigning each firm to one of twenty types. We observe that 955 firms (36.2%) sit below the one-third independent-director threshold and require 1,036 additional directors (948 firms and 1,029 directors backed by board disclosures); that 2,277 firms (86.3%) have a largest-shareholder stake above the 3% audit-election ceiling, with a mean voting-power adjustment of 27.3 percentage points measured on the direct stake alone and therefore a lower bound on the block the rule aggregates; and that board composition clusters on the regulatory minima: 1,170 firms (44.4%) sit at an outside-director ratio of exactly 25% or 33.3%; of the 532 at 33.3%, 38 are legal-minimum defaults with no board disclosure (observed basis 494). Form does not guarantee substance -- of 1,023 firms failing none of the three structural tests -- 43 of which are observed on no structural disclosure at all -- 330 (32.3%) sit outside the resilient quadrant. The directly measurable cost of the package is approximately KRW 68 billion a year and steeply regressive in incidence: 26 of the 28 affected firms with confirmed revenue below KRW 5 billion face a director-procurement cost above 1% of revenue, while no firm with revenue above KRW 50 billion does. The index rests on incomplete behavioural coverage, an observed governance-behaviour score existing for only 42.4% of the frame, and it is a compliance-exposure diagnostic rather than a valuation instrument. The taxonomy exists so that shareholders can identify, firm by firm, which obligations bind and what response each type requires.

title: Simultaneous Determination of Lot Size and RTI Fleet for Series Production: From Sequential to Integrated Optimization

detail.title: Simultaneous Determination of Lot Size and RTI Fleet for Series Production: From Sequential to Integrated Optimization

declarations.declarationOfInterest: There are no competing interests to declare.

detail.abstract: Regulatory and sustainability requirements are encouraging the use of returnable transport items (RTIs), while competitive markets increase cost pressure. Companies must therefore determine the optimal production lot sizes, including RTI-related costs, during the quotation phase for new products. However, the traditional approach of optimizing lot sizes first and subsequently deriving RTI requirements often yields inefficient cost structures. We develop a mixed-integer nonlinear programming (MINLP) model that optimizes production lot sizes and RTI procurement costs, incorporating both rental and investment expenses, considering the complete series production phase of a product. Our approach accounts for fleet shrinkage and optimizes fleet sizes through a novel approach that accounts for return shipments during ongoing production, providing a robust solution to the challenges of RTI fleet and lot size determination. We propose three solution procedures: an enumerative search algorithm, a commercial solver, and a heuristic method, which we apply to use cases of an automotive supplier, and complement with sensitivity analyses to identify key drivers. Our results provide practitioners with a decision support tool for supply chain design to quickly obtain cost-optimal lot sizes and corresponding RTI fleet sizes for individual products and point to promising directions for future research on RTIs and inventory management.

title: DeFi-ying the Fed? Monetary policy transmission to stablecoin deposit rates
affiliations: University of St. Gallen, Banque de France and European Central Bank (ECB) - Directorate General Market Operations

detail.title: DeFi-ying the Fed? Monetary policy transmission to stablecoin deposit rates
detail.abstract: Does the Federal Reserve’s monetary policy influence the rates on USD-pegged stablecoins? While major stablecoin issuers do not pay interest, investors can earn returns by depositing stablecoins in Decentralized Finance (DeFi) protocols. We document unusually large and persistent spreads between traditional short-term interest rates and DeFi deposit rates, as well as a weak and unstable transmission of policy rate changes. We show that, in the short run, monetary policy shocks can move stablecoin rates in the opposite direction of policy rates, delaying a convergence that occurs only over the medium run. Both the sign of the short-run effect and the speed of convergence depend on the intensity of deleveraging induced by crypto-price reactions relative to the standard interest-rate arbitrage channel — an effect shaped by investors’ limited ability to bridge traditional and decentralized finance.

title: Design of an Energy-Efficient Hybrid Neural Network for Beamspace Channel Estimation in 5G Massive MIMO with Metallic Lens Antennas

detail.title: Design of an Energy-Efficient Hybrid Neural Network for Beamspace Channel Estimation in 5G Massive MIMO with Metallic Lens Antennas

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no competing financial or non-financial interests relevant to this work.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no specific external funding and was supported solely by the author's institutional resources.

detail.abstract: Millimeter-wave (mmWave) massive multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) with metallic lens antenna arrays enables beamspace operation, where the spatial channel exhibits inherent sparsity by concentrating energy onto a few dominant beams. While this beamspace transformation drastically reduces the effective channel dimension, accurate estimation remains challenging due to the dynamic nature of user mobility, finite pilot overhead, and the stringent latency constraints of 5G New Radio (NR). Conventional compressed sensing (CS) algorithms, such as orthogonal matching pursuit (OMP), suffer from prohibitively high iterative complexity and sensitivity to parameter tuning, whereas purely data-driven deep learning approaches, despite their enhanced accuracy, incur excessive inference energy that undermines the power budget of baseband processing units. This paper proposes an Energy-Efficient Hybrid Neural Network (EE-HybridNet) for beamspace channel estimation that synergistically integrates model-driven priors with datadriven learning. Specifically, we unroll the iterative shrinkage-thresholding algorithm (ISTA) into a lightweight neural architecture, where the learned measurement matrix and adaptive thresholding modules are jointly optimized to capture the unique phase-delay characteristics of the metallic lens array. To achieve energy efficiency, we introduce a structured pruning strategy coupled with 4-bit quantization during inference, significantly reducing the number of multiply-accumulate (MAC) operations without sacrificing estimation fidelity. Extensive simulations under clustered delay-line (CDL) channel models demonstrate that EE-HybridNet achieves a normalized mean-square error (NMSE) within 0.8 dB of state-of-the-art deep learning baselines, while reducing inference energy consumption by over 73% and computational latency by 5.2× compared to conventional deep unfolding networks. Furthermore, our proposed design exhibits robust performance across varying signal-to-noise ratios (SNR) and mobility-induced beam-switching scenarios, making it a viable candidate for real-time 5G-Advanced and beyond transceivers.

detail.abstract: This paper examines how access to borrower-level credit information affects loan pricing and risk assessment. I focus on the auto loan market, which is dominated by nonbank financial institutions (NBFIs), and exploit the 2019 launch of Israel's national credit registry, which for the first time provided NBFIs with comprehensive borrower-level information. Using variation in registry usage across NBFIs, I implement a difference-indifferences design. Registry adoption reduced interest rate spreads by roughly 0.3 percentage points, with the effect exceeding one percentage point over time. Moreover, it weakened the link between pricing and loan-to-value ratios among highly leveraged loans, indicating a shift from collateral-based toward borrower-level risk pricing. Delinquency rates also declined relative to those of bank lenders. The results provide causal evidence of the impact of credit information in markets characterized by severe informational frictions, with implications for credit market regulation.

detail.abstract: This study analyses the macroeconomic effects of globalization on the growth pattern of Ethiopia from 1992 to 2026 through the structural effects of trade liberalization, efficiency seeking foreign direct investment (FDI), and international migrant remittances. Beyond the binary (Thirlwall's Law), the post-July 2024 market-based unified exchange rate system has triggered a significant structural change that has resulted in a 119.2% increase in export earnings and a 95% decrease in current account deficit up to 2025. At the same time, vertical efficiency seeking FDI in the SEZs reached the all-time high of $4.32 billion in the fiscal year 2025/26. Moreover, formal migrant remittances amounted to $3.30 billion by mid-2026, serving as a very resilient, anti-cyclical, and non-debt financing cushion against severe foreign exchange shortages and balance of payments problems. The paper ends with an optimized framework for macroeconomic governance that aims to protect from the shock effects of currency floating and devaluation.

detail.abstract: This paper studies whether the benefits of prior macroeconomic forecasting experience depend on the state of the economy. In a New Keynesian learning-to-forecast experiment, subjects participate in two consecutive laboratory economies, each with a normal-phase followed by a recession-phase. I use a between-subjects comparison between first-time economies, in which subjects face the laboratory economy for the first time, and experienced economies, in which subjects have prior exposure to a laboratory economy. Experience improves stability in the normal-phase: outcomes remain closer to target, and forecast errors and disagreement are lower. Following the recessionary shock, however, this advantage either largely disappears or reverses. Experienced subjects also adjust inflation forecasts more strongly in the direction opposite to the central bank's inflation target guidance. Individual-level estimates from a heterogeneous-expectations heuristics-switching model suggest that experienced subjects exhibit weaker movement toward mean-reverting forecasting behavior following the recessionary shock. For monetary policy, the results suggest that expectations that appear well anchored in normal times may not be equally resilient to large shocks: prior forecasting experience can support coordination around the target in stable conditions without ensuring that expectations remain anchored under stress.

detail.abstract:
This single-page English legal knowledge graph maps the Supreme People’s Court of China’s Opinions on the Lawful Adjudication of Disputes Involving Artificial Intelligence (Fa Fa [2026] No. 10), issued on 7 September 2026. It integrates provision translations with structured knowledge points drawn from Understanding and Application and the Court’s official press questions and answers. It covers provisions 2–24, with 20 provisions translated in full and excerpts from provisions 2, 23 and 24. The graph connects the 23 displayed provisions to 145 explanatory knowledge points and presents 65 mapped relationships. It covers four main areas: general and specific liability; personality rights and personal information; intellectual property and innovation; and fact-finding and dispute resolution. Cross-references connect issues including model-training data, open-source artificial intelligence, copyright infringement, causation and electronic evidence. The presentation distinguishes the Opinions as judicial guidance from the personal views of the contributors to Understanding and Application and the Court’s official press explanations. Relevant conditions, exceptions and unresolved questions are retained. Arrows indicate analytical or explanatory connections; they do not establish additional legal rules. The contribution is a source-linked visual synthesis that enables readers to trace relationships across the three materials within a single document. All English translations are unofficial.

title: A New Interpretation of the Demographic Transition

detail.title: A New Interpretation of the Demographic Transition

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no competing financial or non-financial interests.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no funding from any agency in the public, commercial or not-for-profit sectors.

detail.abstract:
This paper, written in 2006 was presented at the Conference "Causal Analysis in Population Studies", Vienna, 30 Nov. - 1 Dec. 2006. It is posted here unaltered, and proposes that the demographic transition is a direct consequence of natural selection rather than a sociological regularity in search of a cause. It argues that selection optimises not the number of births but the number of offspring whose arrival at reproductive maturity the progenitor survives to witness — a quantity the paper terms verifiable fitness.

Three consequences follow. Falling child mortality raises rather than lowers the effective price of a birth, because a larger fraction of births now require full investment. Old-age provision and healthcare are purchased from the same budget as children and are deducted first, so societies that succeed at self-survival buy that success partly with gene survival. And the interval between mortality decline and fertility decline is an information-diffusion lag, proportional to linguistic fragmentation and inversely proportional to urbanisation, which predicts that transitions occur in cultural rather than economic units — the central and otherwise awkward finding of the Princeton European Fertility Project.

The paper derives a fertility function, calibrates it across three development levels, and states six testable hypotheses. It predicts convergence toward approximately one child per progenitor dyad rather than toward replacement, on the ground that individually optimal fitness strategies need not preserve the group.

The paper is posted for priority. A companion monograph, The Price of Verification (2026), scores its predictions against the 2006–2026 record, documents where it was wrong, and extends it.

detail.abstract: We ask how an expert panel should disclose auditable conflicts of interest when reports are named and experts care about their reputations for ability. Before sealed binary assessments are filed, an auditor commits to disclosing no orientation information, each named expert's orientation, or only the number of experts oriented in each direction; disclosure occurs after reports are locked. Holding reporting behaviour fixed, composition disclosure and individual attribution are exactly Blackwell-equivalent for learning the state at every finite panel size. Conditional on named reports remaining public, composition is minimal among state-lossless disclosures of orientations: every lossless public message must make the composition recoverable together with the reports. Incentives nevertheless differ sharply. In the large-panel limit near pooling, the local career returns to following evidence against one's orientation under attribution, secrecy, and composition disclosure stand in the ratio 1:4:5. On an open set of parameters, the two extreme regimes have only pooling within symmetric cutoff strategies, while composition disclosure admits a tremble-robust informative equilibrium. Near the lower boundary of this region, a sequence of composition equilibria is sparse—the evidence-following rate is of order 1/N—yet induces a nondegenerate state experiment. Anonymous disclosure can therefore preserve the information available under attribution while creating stronger incentives to produce it.

title:
RETIREMENT EXCHANGE UNDER SEPARATE PUBLIC RESOURCE
CONSTRAINTS

RETIREMENT EXCHANGE UNDER SEPARATE PUBLIC RESOURCE

detail.abstract:
Adjustments to retirement timing place competing demands across multiple public-sector resource accounts. Early retirement can free up payroll spending and open staff positions, yet simultaneously raise pension payout obligations; delayed retirement generates the opposite set of resource outcomes. This paper investigates possible retirement trades under institutional rules that demand each resource account maintain independent feasibility. A key finding concerning pairwise exchange shows that trades may turn out infeasible for every individual supplier-demander pair, even when a larger supplier coalition can satisfy all constraints. Within a setup featuring one demander, three aggregate resource accounts and perfectly divisible, uncapped supply inputs, feasibility for some coalition implies that no more than two suppliers are sufficient to achieve physical feasibility.
We construct a coalition-based mechanism satisfying dominant-strategy incentives,
ex-post individual rationality and exact budget balance. Further, this paper derives
Bayesian implementability conditions built upon allocation monotonicity alongside
a financing requirement rooted in virtual surplus; physical feasibility must hold for
every reported type and every realized allocation outcome. A finite-dimensional
linear programming formulation, paired with a solved bilateral trade benchmark,
enables us to disentangle welfare losses caused by resource limits versus those
stemming from informational rents. Institutional applicability of our theoretical
results is illustrated through time-dated position constraints and a corrected worked
example for paid-leave arrangements. Realizable retirement trades hinge critically
on these preconditions; one cannot simply assume that flexible retirement policies
will self-finance themselves

title: Does AI Exposure Reinforce CEO Overconfidence? Based on 10-K Disclosures and CEO Option Moneyness

detail.title: Does AI Exposure Reinforce CEO Overconfidence? Based on 10-K Disclosures and CEO Option Moneyness

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no competing interests.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding.

detail.abstract:
This study tests whether corporate exposure to artificial intelligence is associated with CEO overconfidence. It also examines whether this relationship varies with CEOs’ pre-existing levels of overconfidence. AI exposure is measured using a textual disclosure index constructed from exact AI-related phrases in firms’ 10-K filings. And CEO overconfidence is tested by the continuous moneyness of unexercised exercisable stock options. The empirical analysis combines ExecuComp, Compustat, corporate filing data. These data cover 4,209 CEO–firm–year observations which represents 1,259 CEOs and 989 firms over fiscal years 2020–2025. CEO outcomes are matched to the most recent eligible 10-K filed before the corresponding option-moneyness measurement date.

All fixed-effects estimates shows that the relationship between AI disclosure and CEO option moneyness is positive but statistically insignificant. However, we find many heterogeneities when CEOs are classified according to their initial observed option moneyness. Among high-baseline CEOs, the estimated AI coefficient becomes progressively larger as the baseline-moneyness threshold increases from 0.67 to 2.00, while the corresponding low-baseline coefficients remain small and generally non-positive. Formal cross-group tests show positive High-minus-Low coefficient differences that increase in magnitude across progressively higher thresholds.

The increasing cross-threshold pattern remains broadly robust to controls for stock-price performance and volatility and to alternative fixed-effect structures. A future-AI placebo test does not reproduce the main cross-group pattern at conventional 5% significance levels. The findings are therefore consistent with a reinforcement interpretation: AI-related corporate exposure may be more strongly associated with subsequent option-retention behavior among CEOs with relatively high baseline option moneyness. The results are interpreted as conditional associations rather than causal effects.

title: Beyond Average Effects in Remote and Hybrid Work Understanding Conditional Outcomes Across Workers, Work and Configurations

detail.title: Beyond Average Effects in Remote and Hybrid Work Understanding Conditional Outcomes Across Workers, Work and Configurations

declarations.declarationOfInterest: No competing interests
declarations.funderStatement: No external funding was received for this work

detail.abstract: Research on remote and hybrid work commonly summarises the consequences of different working conditions through average effects: population-level estimates of the overall direction and magnitude of differences in performance, wellbeing, mental health or other outcomes. Such estimates can be highly informative while still combining materially different conditional effects. Taking Emanuel, Harrington and Pallais's (2026) evidence of heterogeneity by living arrangement as an empirical point of departure, this paper develops a conceptual synthesis of conditional remote and hybrid work outcomes, organised through an analytical architecture comprising three domains: Worker Characteristics and Circumstances, Work Requirements, and Work Location Configuration. Outcomes arise from the relationship among these domains. Configurations change demands, resources and opportunities, and the consequences of those changes depend on the work being performed and on the worker encountering them. Performance, wellbeing and mental health are treated as distinct outcomes that may diverge. Work Location Configuration is specified through features including intensity, discretion, task-location alignment, co-attendance, temporal structure and technological mediation. The paper proposes an evidential progression from population-level effects to theoretically specified heterogeneity, mechanisms, replication and generalisability before differentiated organisational action is justified. The analytical architecture is intended to improve treatment specification and constrain inference while preserving the value of population-level estimates.

title: Prediction Markets as Regulatory Arbitrage

detail.title: Prediction Markets as Regulatory Arbitrage

declarations.declarationOfInterest: n/a

detail.abstract: This Essay provides a unique legal analysis of the rise of prediction platforms such as Kalshi and Polymarket. Due to the recency of commercialized, publicly accessible prediction markets, they are only just now beginning to receive attention in the legal scholarship. Most of the early academic commentary on the subject, however, takes a highly normative slant. The focus is on the costs-and-benefits to society of prediction markets, often through a skeptical lens that emphasizes dysfunctional aspects of prediction markets such as insider trading scandals. By contrast, this essay is agnostic on whether prediction markets are a good or bad thing, and instead examines the particular legal environment that prominent prediction platforms have managed to carve out in order to achieve their booming popularity. That analysis highlights the central role of regulatory arbitrage in shaping the legal landscape of prediction markets, along with the political economy dynamics underlying the contested and still evolving regulatory framework that governs those markets.

detail.abstract: We examine the direct and indirect effects of transparency regulation on economic activity. Using two distinct sources of regulatory variation-the varying extent of financial-reporting requirements and the staggered introduction of electronic business registers in Europe-, we find that direct exposure to transparency regulation tends to hurt focal firms' economic activity (e.g., production and employment). By contrast, we find that indirect exposure to transparency regulation imposed on other related firms tends to help focal firms' economic activity. In terms of relative magnitudes, we find that the negative direct and positive indirect effects tend to be of similar size, almost perfectly offsetting each other. Collectively, our evidence suggests that transparency regulation appears to primarily reallocate economic activity from more toward less regulated markets rather than help or hurt aggregate economic activity.

detail.abstract: In border discontinuity designs, the same economic integration that makes neighboring counties good matches also makes them contaminated controls. We formalize this trade-off and show that the standard population-weighted estimator places nearly half its weight on the most integrated pairs, inflating effective spillover exposure by 80%. Drawing both the treatment and control of each pair from interior counties cuts spillover exposure sevenfold without degrading covariate balance. Interior counterfactuals on both sides increase the estimated income effect of bank branching deregulation by 40%, toward the whole-state benchmark, with roughly half of that shift attributable to the control side alone. In a common minimum-wage specification the bias runs the other way; interior counterfactuals cut the disemployment elasticity by more than half, though neither difference is precisely estimated.

title: Flexible Demand Estimation with Search Data
affiliations: Harvard University - Business School (HBS), Goethe University Frankfurt, University of Toulouse 1 - Toulouse School of Economics (TSE) and Imperial College Business School

detail.title: Flexible Demand Estimation with Search Data
detail.abstract: We propose a model of consideration and choice that uses search data to flexibly estimate co-search patterns for every pair of products. Using simulations, we show that estimating co-search flexibly rather than modeling the drivers of consideration comes at a modest cost in precision but guards against misspecification. The method is therefore particularly valuable in online markets, where the drivers of consideration — such as webpage layout or product recommendations — are often unobserved. Relative to using purchase data alone, search data substantially improves the precision of cross-price elasticity estimates, because products that are searched together tend to be close substitutes and because browsing data is far more abundant than purchases. We apply our approach to data from an online retailer and find that most products have a small set of close substitutes and that accounting for substitution patterns when setting prices raises the retailer's average mark-up from 36.5% to 47.5% and increases its profits.

title: Voice AI in Firms: A Natural Field Experiment on Automated Job Interviews
affiliations: and Erasmus University Rotterdam

detail.title: Voice AI in Firms: A Natural Field Experiment on Automated Job Interviews
detail.abstract: We study AI agents as information-collection technologies: automated systems that elicit decision-relevant signals from humans through live interactions. We test how such AI automation impacts information collection and organizational outcomes using a natural field experiment with 70,000 applicants applying for real jobs. Applicants were randomly assigned to be interviewed by either human recruiters or AI voice agents. Afterward, human recruiters evaluate the interviews and make hiring decisions. Applicants interviewed by AI agents are 12% more likely to receive job offers, and these gains translate into higher job starts and worker retention, with no decline in the productivity of hired workers. Analyzing interview transcripts reveals that AI voice agents achieve controlled variance: their interviews are more structured and consistent while remaining responsive to individual applicants, which is associated with more hiring-relevant information collected. Our results suggest that a key advantage of AI automation lies in environments where information collection is delegated across many human workers and repeated such that variance in task execution becomes noise in decision-relevant signals, which AI compresses through adaptive standardization.

title: Tax Sovereignty and Investor Protection: Why the Proposed Global Minimum Tax Is Not the Final Frontier for Corporate Tax Arbitrage

detail.title: Tax Sovereignty and Investor Protection: Why the Proposed Global Minimum Tax Is Not the Final Frontier for Corporate Tax Arbitrage

keywords: Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD)

detail.abstract: Over the past decade, international tax governance has evolved with bewildering speed in response to the challenges of digitalization and widespread corporate tax avoidance. Since the launch of the Group of 20 (G20)-Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD) base erosion and profit shifting (BEPS) initiative in 2012, 135 countries and 14 international organizations have joined the BEPS Inclusive Framework, committing to implement new global standards on corporate tax, which has already been lauded as a revolution in the architecture of international tax law and policy. Even further expanding the scope of the OECD's work on international taxation in a landmark announcement in March 2021, the U.S. administration further proposed imposing a global minimum corporate tax at a rate of 21% to be implemented through an international agreement by mid-2021. If the new OECD initiative is agreed, will the plan to implement a minimum corporate tax be fully implemented by G20 members, and if so, will it do enough to address the tax challenges of digitalization embodied in corporate tax arbitrage? Although the evidence suggests legislative and public policy compliance is likely to be high among G20 members, this article argues the minimum tax initiative is unlikely to go far enough to address deficiencies in global tax dispute resolution, which are extremely germane to the success of the proposed minimum tax. As explained in this article, U.S. leaders and global policymakers must enhance the mutual agreement procedure (MAP), a cornerstone of tax dispute resolution, given a growing body of tax litigation in investment law that threatens the implementation of BEPS 2.0. To do so, global policymakers must also reconcile the conflict of norms between tax sovereignty and investor protection contained in the investor-state dispute settlement (ISDS) regime. Only by addressing the conflict between the principles of tax sovereignty and investor protection can they prevent a potential tidal wave of investor disputes that will challenge the implementation of the minimum tax through national tax laws.

detail.abstract: This study examines how local government fiscal stress shapes corporate payout policies when governments hold control rights over firms. Using a sample of China's listed local state-owned enterprises (SOEs) from 2003 to 2024, we find that local land revenue shortfalls significantly raise dividend payouts. This effect is more pronounced where local governments have greater ability and incentives to extract corporate resources, including firms with higher state ownership and in regions with greater dependence on land finance, higher local debt pressure, and stronger political influence. We further find that higher dividend payouts are followed by increased government procurement, suggesting that firms may receive compensating benefits from local governments. However, these payouts are also associated with lower innovation investment and reduced employee compensation. Overall, our findings show that local fiscal stress can be transmitted to corporate financial policies through government control, highlighting a trade-off between short-term fiscal relief for local governments and long-term corporate development.

title: Reactions to Grades
affiliations: Autonomous University of Barcelona, , University of Florida and University of Florida

detail.title: Reactions to Grades

declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding.

detail.abstract: We study how students respond to grades using random assignment of anonymized writing assignments to graders in two large introductory economics courses. Although all graders use the same rubric and grading guidelines, they differ systematically in leniency, generating exogenous variation in grades within the same course and assignment. Students who receive higher grader-induced grades contest them less, perceive the grading as more lenient, and become more overconfident about the next assignment. These higher grades partly undo themselves as approximately a quarter of the gain is offset by lower performance on the next assignment. However, exam confidence and performance are unchanged. Students appear to treat grades as task-specific signals about grading standards rather than as broad signals about overall course performance. These findings provide evidence that the perception of low grading standards can harm students.

title: Precarious Augmentation in the Age of AI: Task Bottlenecks and Organizational Tipping

detail.title: Precarious Augmentation in the Age of AI: Task Bottlenecks and Organizational Tipping

declarations.declarationOfInterest: No interests to delcare.

detail.abstract: The same improvement in AI capability can make human work more valuable and more vulnerable to automation. This paper develops a task-based model of structural change within jobs. Jobs are bundles of tasks, each task can be supplied by humans or AI, and firms choose both task assignments and organizational production modes. A CES production technology creates within-job complementarities: when some tasks automate in jobs with low substitution elasticities, remaining human tasks become bottlenecks whose shadow values rise. This is augmentation in the mixed human-AI regime. But the premium is precarious. By raising the shadow value of human task capacity, AI can also increase the incentive to automate those same tasks and push the job toward AI-only production. Mode-specific organizational overheads generate two thresholds: adoption of the AI operation and shutdown of the human operation. The model therefore produces a rise-then-cliff path in which AI first raises the value of remaining human tasks and then eliminates them when the job tips into AI-only production. The welfare framework weights human income and domestically captured AI-sector income separately, subtracts transition costs, and distinguishes three margins of technological change: deepening, widening, and tipping. These margins yield policy-screening conditions for human training, task-specific AI investment, and caution toward "so-so" automation. The model also generates testable predictions that distinguish it from canonical task models and occupational exposure indices.

title: From the Other End: Offender-side Evidence from Fraud Call Centres Targeting US and UK Victims

detail.title: From the Other End: Offender-side Evidence from Fraud Call Centres Targeting US and UK Victims

detail.abstract:
The literature on transnational call-centre fraud has been written almost entirely from one side of it. Victim-country research draws on reported losses, victimisation surveys, financial-institution records and infrastructure telemetry-all abundant where the victims are, none of which reach the premises where the fraud is performed. The offender end sits in a jurisdiction that victim-country researchers cannot enter and victim-country police cannot police. The result is a field with detailed knowledge of the harm and comparatively little of the enterprise producing it. 

This paper reports from inside the offender jurisdiction. It draws on six enforcement operations conducted between August 2023 and August 2025 in the Gautam Buddh Nagar Police Commissionerate, in India's National Capital Region, which dismantled fraudulent call centres targeting victims in the United States and United Kingdom and produced more than 280 arrests. The author held supervisory charge of crime in that commissionerate during part of the period. 

The paper makes four arguments. First, that these operations are better understood as workplaces than as networks, extending existing accounts of cybercrime industrialisation and division of labour from online settings to the physical, staffed premises, and permitting a crime-script reconstruction built from seized training material rather than inferred from victim accounts. Second, that the labour supply is patterned and locatable: arrest records disclose two geographically distinct recruitment pools, a concentration of operators in their late teens and early twenties, and residential clustering consistent with organised recruitment. Third, that technical infrastructure persists while operators do not-the same dialling software recurs across three years and four organisationally unconnected operations, locating the model's inelastic point. Fourth, that victim selection constitutes deliberate engineering of guardian absence: the offenders in one case explained that they chose foreign nationals precisely so that nobody could attend their premises to complain, which reframes the enforcement asymmetry from structural condition to design decision.

detail.abstract: This chapter explores the inherent tension between regulatory contract law, understood as the instrumental use of private law to achieve exogenous social, economic, or environmental goals, and the mobility of legal subjects in a globalised legal order. Utilising the conceptual framework of a 'market for contract law', the analysis distinguishes between demand-side regulatory arbitrage, where private actors exploit the high elasticity of contract law to minimise regulatory costs, and supply-side regulatory competition, where states act as producers of legal rules. The chapter identifies a structural paradox: the more a jurisdiction employs contract law for regulatory purposes, the greater the incentive it creates for parties to exit that regime, potentially undermining the very policy objectives the law seeks to advance. However, the analysis suggests that a 'race to the bottom' in regulatory standards as integral parts of contract law is not inevitable. It argues that jurisdictions are shifting from adaptive competition 'on the merits' toward strategies of 'marketaccess bundling', effectively constraining the elasticity of demand by conditioning market entry on regulatory compliance.

title: Personal Accounting Climate Economic (P.A.C.E.) System: A Phase 1 Design and Empirical Validation Study for Localizing the Sustainable Development Goals

detail.title: Personal Accounting Climate Economic (P.A.C.E.) System: A Phase 1 Design and Empirical Validation Study for Localizing the Sustainable Development Goals

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares that they have no known competing financial interests or personal relationships that could have appeared to influence the work reported in this paper. The P.A.C.E. architecture and computational modules discussed represent an independent academic design-science research model.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Formal ethical approval for this large-sample survey study was officially granted by the Maynooth University Research Ethics Committee via the centralized institutional Research Information System (RIS). Informed consent was obtained electronically from all 504 participants prior to data collection, and strict data anonymization protocols were enforced in accordance with GDPR mandates.
declarations.funderStatement: This research was conducted as part of a postdoctoral fellowship at the Innovation Value Institute, Maynooth University. This work was supported and co-funded by the European Commission under the Horizon Europe Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions (MSCA) co-funding scheme, specifically through the DIGI+ Global Postdoctoral Fellowship programme (Project ID: 101081609, DIGI PLUS).

detail.abstract: Localising the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) at the individual level requires mobilising sustained behaviour change within complex social and institutional systems, yet effective mechanisms for this challenge remain underdeveloped. Higher Education Institutions (HEIs), as living laboratories for sustainability transitions, provide a compelling context for addressing this gap. This paper presents a Phase 1 design and empirical validation study for the Personal Accounting Climate Economic (P.A.C.E.) system, a transdisciplinary service model integrating: (1) customised sustainability activities for persona-specific habit formation; (2) a Q-learning reinforcement learning (RL) module for adaptive activity selection; (3) a Modern Portfolio Theory (MPT) economic module to quantify activity synergies and trade-offs; (4) a gamified reward system; and (5) a master database for real-time SDG impact tracking. A survey of 504 students across 32 departments at Maynooth University validates user needs, behavioural barriers, and incentive preferences  across seven empirically derived sustainability persona groups. One-way ANOVA confirms statistically significant differences in touchpoint preferences, activity needs, and reward responsiveness across groups (p < 0.05). Tukey HSD post-hoc comparisons identify that Inactive and Frontrunner groups differ significantly on touchpoint preference (p = 0.003) and feature demand (p = 0.008). Computational simulations of the RL and MPT modules demonstrate persona-differentiated optimal activity portfolios and algorithmic convergence, providing design-science validation without requiring full deployment. A structured feature comparison confirms P.A.C.E. scores 23/24 capability dimensions versus a maximum of 12/24 for existing tools. This Phase 1 study delivers the empirical foundation and architectural blueprint for Phase 2 prototype deployment, currently in progress.

title: Democratizing Private Markets? A First Look at European Long-Term Investment Funds

detail.title: Democratizing Private Markets? A First Look at European Long-Term Investment Funds

declarations.declarationOfInterest: Nothing to disclose.
declarations.funderStatement: Financial support from the Dutch Research Council (NWO) through SSH Open Competition XS grant 406.XS.26.01.060 is gratefully acknowledged.

detail.abstract: The European Long-Term Investment Fund (ELTIF) is the European Union's vehicle for opening private markets to retail investors. I hand-collect fee schedules, liquidity terms, and return disclosures for 162 funds and 746 share classes from over 1,000 regulatory documents. ELTIF fees are private-markets fees: twice the ongoing cost of an active mutual fund and, all-in, more than ten times an index fund. Funds sell one portfolio through several share classes at prices that differ by investor: fees fall with the class's minimum investment, and retail classes pay 60 basis points per year more than institutional classes of the same fund. This retail wedge compensates distribution rather than liquidity, and retail money does not reach the cheaper classes that most funds post. On their own projections, four in five retail classes trail a plain index fund, while the regulated disclosures rate gated private-debt ELTIFs like daily-dealing bond funds. Finally, the section of the mandated disclosure that describes the product falls short of the readability standard US states apply to insurance policies.

title: Corridor Invoicing: Real Hedging in International Trade
affiliations: Sapienza University of Rome, University of Bologna, Boston College and Boston College - Department of Economics

detail.title: Corridor Invoicing: Real Hedging in International Trade

declarations.declarationOfInterest: All authors declare no conflicts of interest.

detail.abstract: Using the universe of Italian customs from 2000 to 2021, matched to firm balancesheets, we study how invoicing currency shapes exchange-rate exposure and profitability for two-sided trading firms. We document four facts. First, when a firm begins invoicing imports in dollars, it becomes far more likely to invoice exports in dollars the same year, with import-side adoption leading. Second, this matching is bilateral: a firm importing from a country in dollars disproportionately invoices exports to that country in dollars, a corridor structure that aggregate hedging cannot rationalize. Third, corridor alignment reduces profit variance beyond what aggregate net dollar exposure explains. Fourth, exchange-rate movements transmit to profits mainly through transactions rather than balance-sheet revaluation, and dollar-invoiced import quantities rise after a euro depreciation, concentrated in inputs linked to exports. We interpret these facts through a model of invoicing currency choice with a rich sourcing and export destination structure, driven by price-stability motives and the incentive to hedge country-specific risk. In the richest framework, invoicing currency choice is a real hedge against country risk, not only currency risk.

title: Does Income Explain Cross-Country Plastic Pollution? A Regression Analysis of 204 Countries, with a Focus on Pakistan

detail.title: Does Income Explain Cross-Country Plastic Pollution? A Regression Analysis of 204 Countries, with a Focus on Pakistan

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no conflicts of interest.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding and was conducted independently by the author.

detail.abstract: Plastic pollution is typically reported and discussed in absolute national totals, a framing that largely reflects population size rather than a country's underlying capacity to manage waste. This paper asks a narrower and more policy-relevant question: does a country's income level predict how much plastic pollution it generates per person? Using Our World in Data's crosscountry plastic pollution estimates (Cottom et al., 2024) merged with GDP per capita and population data for 2020, this study runs two ordinary least squares regressions across 204 countries. A first model regressing total plastic pollution on GDP per capita finds no meaningful relationship (R² = 0.007), confirming that raw pollution totals are driven primarily by population rather than income. Recasting the outcome as pollution per capita changes the picture substantially: GDP per capita is a highly significant negative predictor of pollution per capita (coefficient =-1.804e-07, p < 0.001), and income alone explains roughly half of the crosscountry variation (R² = 0.505). Pakistan's pollution per capita is closely in line with what its income level would predict, and is comparable to Bangladesh despite Bangladesh's considerably higher income, while Nigeria emerges as a clear positive outlier relative to the income-pollution trend. These findings suggest that incomelinked waste management infrastructure, rather than income itself, is likely the operative mechanism, with direct implications for how low-and middle-income countries such as Pakistan might prioritize investment in waste collection and management systems.

title: GENCO — A Unified Neural Solver Embedded in a Development Framework for Steady-state Grid Analysis
affiliations: IBM Research Europe - Zurich, IBM Research Europe - Zurich, IBM Research Europe - Zurich, IBM Research Europe - Zurich, IBM Research Europe - Zurich, Hydro-Québec, University of Montreal, Hydro-Québec, IBM Research Europe - Zurich, IBM Research Europe - Zurich, IBM Research Europe - Zurich, IBM Research Europe - Zurich, IBM Research Europe - Zurich, ETH Zürich - Reliability and Risk Engineering Laboratory, ETH Zürich, affiliation not provided to SSRN, IBM Research Europe - Zurich, IBM Research Europe - Zurich, Hydro-Québec, State University of New York (SUNY), Stony Brook, IBM Research Europe - Zurich and IBM Research Europe - Zurich

detail.title: GENCO — A Unified Neural Solver Embedded in a Development Framework for Steady-state Grid Analysis
detail.abstract:
Foundation models are transforming business workflows and boosting productivity, yet they remain noticeably absent from some engineering domains such as power system analysis, where strict physical consistency must be enforced.

We present GENCO (GEometric Neural Corrective Optimizer), a unified neural solver for steady-state transmission grid analysis that handles power flow (PF), optimal power flow (OPF), and state estimation (SE) within a single architecture, eliminating task-specific pipelines by operating on a shared grid representation. To support advances in neural power system solvers, we introduce the open-source GridFM Development Framework that standardizes synthetic data generation and training in a low-code environment. We also release large-scale datasets with millions of PF and OPF scenarios across diverse grid topologies to further support reproducible benchmarking.We evaluate GENCO on the latest benchmark datasets (PF∆, OPFData), against all current state-of-the-art neural solvers, as well as classical solvers (Newton–Raphson, IPOPT) and real-world Hydro-Québec SCADA data. For large-scale PF, GENCO recovers the full AC operating state—including voltage magnitudes and reactive power that DC-PF cannot provide—while matching DC-PF-level active power-balance residuals, with up to 30× speedups over Newton–Raphson at only 2× the runtime of DC-PF. For OPF, it achieves up to 85× speedups over IPOPT while improving feasibility, optimality, and runtime over DC-OPF. For SE, it is more robust than classical weighted least squares (WLS) to noisy measurements and grid parameters, and it always returns a high-quality estimate even when WLS fails to converge.Together, the unified architecture and development framework offer a new way to perform large-scale steady-state grid analysis, reduce integration effort, and lower the barrier to entry for power system engineers, marking a key step toward Grid Foundation Models.

title: The Collateral Illusion: Real versus Nominal Collateral and Default in Turkish Auto Lending

detail.title: The Collateral Illusion: Real versus Nominal Collateral and Default in Turkish Auto Lending

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author provides consulting services to the Turkish auto finance company whose anonymized loan-level data are used in this study, through an independent consulting arrangement. No other financial or personal relationships that could be perceived to have influenced this research are declared.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This study uses anonymized, loan-level administrative data obtained through the author's consulting relationship with the data-providing institution. No borrower-identifying information was accessed, and the study involved no human-subject interaction, survey, or intervention. As such, formal ethics committee/IRB approval was not applicable.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no specific grant from any funding agency in the public, commercial, or not-for-profit sectors.

detail.abstract: We document a collateral illusion in auto lending under high inflation. Using proprietary loan-level data from a large Turkish auto finance company over 2019-2026, a period of extreme inflation and a vehicle-price boom and bust, we show that the nominal collateral values commonly used by lenders can generate misleading risk signals. Measured nominally, the collateral index for used-car loans correlates positively with the segment NPL ratio (+0.53), a counterintuitive pattern; deflating by the consumer price index restores a consistent negative relationship in both new-and used-car segments. The pattern holds at the level of the individual loan, conditional on standard credit-risk controls and robust to vintage fixed effects, clustered standard errors, and the choice of horizon. Decomposing the effect shows that it is largely systematic, operating through the market-wide collateral cycle rather than vehicle-specific variation, so that it cannot be fully diversified away within the vehicle portfolio and must be managed at that level. A wedge between book and transaction values shows the illusion is present even at origination, before any real erosion. The real-collateral signal also carries operational value as an early-warning input, most of all at the earliest stage of a loan's life, where a lender still has room to act. In high-inflation economies, the real-versus-nominal measurement of collateral is therefore first-order for credit risk.

title: The Road to a Distant Goal: Self-Control, Self-Awareness, and Dynamic Effort Incentives
affiliations: Monash University - Department of Economics and Monash University - Department of Economics

detail.title: The Road to a Distant Goal: Self-Control, Self-Awareness, and Dynamic Effort Incentives

detail.abstract: Beliefs about future self-control affect whether a person works toward a distant goal or leaves the task to a later self. We study when imperfect self-knowledge can improve this decision. In a four-date completion problem, an intermediate range of forecasts induces immediate completion, whereas both full sophistication and full naivete induce delay. The intermediate forecasts attain the full first best along the realized path, and the result holds on an open set of primitives. A complementary cumulative-effort model characterizes the marginal continuation-value wedge through which self-forecasts affect current effort. It distinguishes efficient current action from efficient behavior throughout the project. Under strict present bias, forecasts cannot remove underinvestment at either of the final two nonterminal dates, and beliefs alone cannot implement the full first-best effort path. The analysis identifies the scope and limits of functional beliefs without assuming that individuals can freely choose their beliefs or that feedback sustains them. Immediate rewards can address distortions that self-awareness cannot.

title: Decision-Adjusted Dependence: AI Assignment, Model Migration, and Price Discovery

declarations.ethicsApproval: NA
