detail.abstract: This study examines how double-entry bookkeeping (DEB) functions as an accountability structure in partnership settings. Historical and social-scientific debates link DEB to the expansion of economic activity, but evidence remains limited on the behavioural mechanisms through which DEB-type information structures affect investment and allocation decisions. Using a partnership-based economic experiment, the study compares single-entry bookkeeping (SEB)-type and DEB-type information environments. Participants were paired in a repeated joint-investment task in which both partners invested in a joint business and one managing partner allocated the resulting distribution pool. The manipulation concerned the accounting information available within the allocation process. In the SEB-type environment, the distribution pool and amounts allocated to each partner were shown; in the DEB-type environment, this information was supplemented by each partner’s contribution, the multiplier, and resulting profit. The results do not provide evidence that DEB directly increases total investment. However, the DEB-type environment is robustly associated with smaller deviations between Distribution Share and Investment Share. The association between deviation from proportional allocation and next-round total investment is negative under conventional pair-clustered inference, but is not robust to wild cluster bootstrap inference. Mediation analysis provides descriptive evidence of a possible positive indirect pathway through reduced deviation from proportional allocation, rather than definitive evidence of a statistically robust causal mediation process. These findings suggest that DEB matters less by directly promoting investment than by organizing the informational conditions under which proportional allocation becomes a meaningful reference point for accountable allocation decisions.

title: The Stratified Three-Agent Tractable Economy (STATE) Model: When a Third Household Dimension is Necessary

detail.title: The Stratified Three-Agent Tractable Economy (STATE) Model: When a Third Household Dimension is Necessary

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no competing interests.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding.

detail.abstract: Low-dimensional heterogeneous-household models provide a tractable alternative to richer heterogeneousagent models by retaining a small number of household types while preserving selected distributional mechanisms. Their usefulness, however, depends on whether the retained household dimensions contain the information required for the economic outcome being studied. When a two-dimensional householdincome state is summarized by two locally independent statistics, those statistics generically exhaust the state, leaving no additional distributional direction that can vary independently. This creates a model-design problem: when does adding a third household dimension preserve genuinely new economic information rather than merely add another household category? I develop the Stratified Three-Agent Tractable Economy (STATE) to identify the first dimension beyond that boundary. With three household-income dimensions and two independent retained statisticsaggregate disposable income and aggregate consumption-I show that exactly one residual stratification direction generically remains. The third dimension is economically necessary if and only if the target outcome loads on that direction. Applying the result to Distributionally Weighted Investment, I show that two household-income allocations can generate identical aggregate disposable income and aggregate consumption yet different desired productive investment when the investment-weight vector contains a component outside the span of the aggregate-income and marginal-propensity-to-consume directions. More generally, when K independent statistics summarize an N-dimensional heterogeneous state, one residual direction first becomes possible at N = K + 1. STATE therefore provides an outcome-specific criterion for determining when a two-type model is sufficient, when a third household dimension is warranted, and when richer heterogeneity is necessary.

title: "Till death do us part": Easier Access to Divorce and Femicide
affiliations: , Catholic University of the Sacred Heart of Milan and

detail.title: "Till death do us part": Easier Access to Divorce and Femicide

declarations.declarationOfInterest: None declared.
declarations.funderStatement: Davide Cipullo gratefully acknowledges financial support from Unicredit Foundation and Marco Fanno Association Modigliani Research Grant 2023. Elisa Muscarella acknowledges the support of the Joan Oró FI predoctoral grant program of the Department of Research and Universities of the Government of Catalonia, co-financed by the European Social Fund Plus (No. 2025 FI-1 00607).

detail.abstract: This paper estimates the causal effect of easing access to divorce on domestic violence. We study two legislative reforms in Italy that sharply cut the monetary costs and mandatory waiting periods for divorce, triggering a large and heterogeneous rise in divorce rates nationwide. We combine administrative data on the universe of divorces with a novel dataset on femicides, and we exploit plausibly exogenous variation in municipalities' exposure to the reforms, arising from municipalities' age composition interacted with national age-specific divorce rates. We find that easier access to divorce increases the probability of femicide, an effect primarily driven by domestic cases. We also find a reduction in measures typically associated with non-lethal domestic violence, indicating that lethal and non-lethal violence need not respond in the same way to an improvement in women's outside options.

title:
LAMINAR: 
Measuring an Order-flow Coherence Label across Twelve Futures Instruments

detail.title:
LAMINAR: 
Measuring an Order-flow Coherence Label across Twelve Futures Instruments

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author is the developer of LAMINAR, the system evaluated in this study, and is affiliated with Davis Geometric. No other competing interests are declared.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable. This study analyzes market-event data and does not involve human-participant recruitment, clinical research, or interventions.
declarations.funderStatement: This research was self-funded by the author and received no external grants or sponsorship.

detail.abstract:
We evaluate LAMINAR, a session-relative order-flow classifier, to measure the incidence, perturbation sensitivity and context dependence of its coherence label. A fixed configuration is evaluated on a common numerical price scale across 15 futures tapes representing 12 instruments, 36,533,928 trades and 194 trading-day sessions. Its LAMINAR label appears in every included session, with pooled incidence from 6.35% to 9.67% among non-initializing reporting observations. 

Incidence alone does not identify market-specific organization. A control grid of 70 executions covers seven source sessions in four instruments. Surrogates that independently resample session marginals produce mean incidence at least as high as the real inputs in three of those instruments. The tested S&P session shows a larger response to price-path permutation: incidence falls from 7.94% to 4.92%-5.56% across two seeds. 

Selection within inserted episodes provides a different measurement. Grafted real segments have higher mean inside than outside incidence on gold and the S&P, but lower mean inside incidence on yen and the 2-year Treasury future. Synthetic episodes yield a different pattern. These results distinguish frequency of selection, sensitivity to the chosen perturbation, and retention of a label in a changed context. A separate controlled replay also shows why price representation and withheld classifications must be recorded explicitly. The findings concern the measurement and its controls; predictive returns, execution performance and the classifier's proprietary construction are outside the study's scope.

title: Kidnapping for Ransom in Nigeria: Drivers Dynamics and Transnational Security Implications
affiliations: National Defence College, Nigeria

detail.title: Kidnapping for Ransom in Nigeria: Drivers Dynamics and Transnational Security Implications

declarations.declarationOfInterest: none
declarations.ethicsApproval: none
declarations.funderStatement: none

detail.abstract: Kidnapping for ransom has become one of the most visible manifestations of insecurity in Nigeria, but it remains analytically under-specified. It is frequently described either as ordinary criminality or as an extension of jihadist violence. Neither account adequately explains a phenomenon in which bandit groups, insurgent factions, community intermediaries, markets, family networks, state officials and digital platforms interact across multiple regions. This article examines the drivers, operational dynamics and consequences of kidnapping for ransom in Nigeria between 2021 and 2026. It uses a qualitative comparative design and a descriptive time-series reconstruction of publicly reported incidents, ransom demands, confirmed payments, release outcomes and payment modalities. The reconstruction combines official statements, court and policy materials, credible media reports, ACLED event data, humanitarian reporting and successive open-source datasets produced by SBM Intelligence. It treats under-reporting and inconsistent attribution as findings rather than measurement errors to be ignored. The analysis shows a shift from episodic, elite-targeted abduction to a diversified coercive economy affecting schools, religious institutions, highways, farms, campuses, extractive sites and urban peripheries. The most reliable national series records 3,620 abducted persons in July 2022–June 2023, 4,722 in July 2024–June 2025, and 7,825 in July 2025–June 2026; the discontinuity itself reflects the absence of a public, audited national registry. Kidnapping persists because expected returns are high, risks of detection and prosecution are low, borderland sanctuaries and illicit markets lower operating costs, and families face an acute moral imperative to negotiate. The article argues that prohibition of ransom payment, without victim-protection arrangements, financial intelligence, accountable rescue capacity and local prevention, may push transactions further into secrecy. It proposes a national kidnapping observatory, a victim-centred reporting and negotiation protocol, financial-disruption measures, corridor and school protection, accountable policing, and Nigeria-led regional cooperation with Sahelian neighbours. The study speaks to international debates on hostagetaking by showing how a criminal market becomes embedded in a broader ecosystem of governance failure, armed mobilisation and transnational insecurity.

title: Patents, Pay and People: How Innovation Reshapes the Workforce
affiliations: , Middle East Technical University (METU) - Department of Economics and Middle East Technical University - Department of Economics

detail.title: Patents, Pay and People: How Innovation Reshapes the Workforce
detail.abstract: We examine how innovation shapes firm-level workforce dynamics using rich administrative data from Türkiye, a developing economy characterized by medium-technology, incremental innovation. We find that patent-based innovation increases both firm size and average daily wages, with the largest employment gains among workers earning just above the median wage. To uncover the mechanisms behind these outcomes, we construct worker transition matrices. Relative to comparable non-innovative firms, innovative firms (i) retain incumbent workers at higher rates, particularly at the top of the wage distribution, (ii) promote retained workers into higher wage bins more frequently, and (iii) hire more new workers, disproportionately into higher wage bins. Finally, occupational composition analysis shows that employment growth is concentrated among technical and production occupations, consistent with the medium-technology, incremental nature of innovation in our sample.

title: Algorithmic Litigation Finance and Civil Justice Market Integrity

detail.title: Algorithmic Litigation Finance and Civil Justice Market Integrity

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author developed the Algorithmic Litigation Finance Accountability Framework, the Algorithmic Funding Disclosure and Integrity Test, and the proposed future AI-assisted implementation pathway examined in this article. This role creates a potential risk of confirmation bias. To manage this risk, the associated validation programme has been prospectively registered and incorporates multidisciplinary stakeholder participation, independent expert review, standardised instruments, prespecified analysis, documented human-review procedures, version control, and transparent reporting of convergent, divergent, and critical findings. The author has no financial interest in any litigation-funding arrangement assessed in this article Affiliation and Independence The author is an independent researcher and author and serves as Founder and Principal Consultant of Right4Tun Business Consultants Ltd. This article was prepared in the author’s independent scholarly capacity. Right4Tun Business Consultants Ltd did not sponsor, direct, review, or fund the research. The views expressed are solely those of the author and should not be attributed to any former professional or organisational affiliation.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This article is a conceptual, doctrinal, and normative legal study. It does not involve human participants, patients, personal data, biological materials, interventions, surveys, interviews, or the collection or analysis of original empirical data. Accordingly, institutional ethics approval and participant consent were not required. Any future stakeholder validation or empirical research will be conducted separately under the prospectively registered protocol and will commence only after obtaining applicable institutional ethics approval or a formal exemption.
declarations.funderStatement: No external funding was received for the preparation of this article.

detail.abstract: Civil litigation is increasingly becoming a financial market in which claims are identified, screened, valued, funded, insured, bundled, settled, and monetised. Third-party litigation finance has already generated policy concern around disclosure, funder identity, settlement influence, litigation control, foreign funding, class actions, and mass torts. Artificial intelligence intensifies these concerns by making claim origination, damages modelling, settlement prediction, document review, demand generation, and portfolio investment faster, cheaper, and less visible. This article argues that litigation finance transparency must therefore evolve into algorithmic litigation finance accountability. Building on the author’s parent proposal, The Civil Justice Integrity Screening Framework for Litigation Abuse and Institutional Accountability, this article develops the finance-facing branch of that broader civil justice integrity project. It proposes the Algorithmic Litigation Finance Accountability Framework, a seven-domain model for evaluating AI-enabled litigation finance across claim origination integrity, funding transparency, algorithmic control risk, portfolio distortion risk, evidence and damages reliability, settlement pressure and bargaining fairness, and access-to-justice protection. The article then operationalises the framework through the Algorithmic Funding Disclosure and Integrity Test, a five-question assessment tool designed to identify whether an AI-enabled litigation finance arrangement appears legitimate or low-risk, moderate-risk, high-risk, or in need of enhanced human review. The article further presents the functional and governance foundations of the Algorithmic Funding Disclosure, AI Assessment, and Integrity Classification Model. A complete clickable working prototype and a confidential technical implementation specification have already been developed as integral components of the same research programme. The prototype demonstrates structured intake, supporting-document categorisation, rule-based pre-assessment, evidence and damages traceability, provisional risk indicators, red-flag identification, human-review routing, report generation, and audit logging. The framework and five-question operational test will first undergo stakeholder validation to assess clarity, content validity, reproducibility, proportionality, usability, balance, and access-to-justice safeguards. The validation findings will be used to confirm or refine the framework elements already operationalised in the prototype. The refined prototype will then undergo controlled model testing, initially with synthetic, public, anonymised, or permission-based materials and subsequently with real documents only where lawful access, applicable ethics approval or exemption, confidentiality and privilege protections, privacy and security requirements, and appropriate data-governance arrangements are in place. Controlled testing will assess technical reliability, human-review performance, implementation readiness, and scalability before any consideration of institutional deployment. The companion protocol, Feasibility and Scalability Protocol for Algorithmic Legal Finance Integrity, was prospectively registered on the Open Science Framework under embargo before data collection and specifies the framework-validation methodology.

title: Optimal Taxation with Migration and Regional Externalities
affiliations: Middle East Technical University (METU) - Department of Economics

detail.title: Optimal Taxation with Migration and Regional Externalities
detail.abstract: This paper studies optimal taxation when marginal contributions to an externality differ between urban and rural regions (non-atmospheric externalities), and individuals can migrate from rural to urban regions to earn higher wages. I show that when the government is constrained to set a uniform commodity tax across regions, the presence of externalities alters the structure of optimal redistribution. In particular, if, for example, urban residents impose higher marginal external damages, the optimal policy features more redistribution, relative to a benchmark without externalities. This additional redistribution reduces the attractiveness of higher urban wages and thus discourages migration into the urban region. These findings highlight a potential role for redistributive policy in internalizing externalities.

title: Consensus Without Commitment: Enlargement, Declaratory Output and the Weakening of Security Language in the 2026 BRICS New Delhi Declaration

detail.title: Consensus Without Commitment: Enlargement, Declaratory Output and the Weakening of Security Language in the 2026 BRICS New Delhi Declaration

declarations.declarationOfInterest: Not Affiliated with any other individual or body
declarations.funderStatement: Self Funded

detail.abstract: Purpose. This paper asks whether the enlargement of BRICS from five to eleven members has strengthened or weakened the group's capacity to take positions on contested security questions, and what that answer implies for the public policy objectives India pursues through the grouping. Methodology. The study uses structured textual comparison of two primary documents, the Rio de Janeiro Declaration adopted in July 2025 and the New Delhi Declaration adopted on 12 September 2026, supported by a five-summit series of declaration lengths running from Beijing in 2022 to New Delhi in 2026. Commitment strength is coded along four observable dimensions: the governing verb, the legal characterisation of conduct, whether any state is named, and the presence of a reservation clause. Findings. Declaratory output has grown steadily, from 75 numbered paragraphs at Beijing in 2022 to 140 at New Delhi in 2026. Commitment strength on the single security question that most directly affects a member state has moved in the opposite direction. On Iran, the 2025 text condemned military strikes and characterised them as a violation of international law. The 2026 text, written during an active war involving that same member, drops the condemnation, names no party, and inserts an explicit reservation recalling respective national positions. Language on Palestine, Cuba and institutional reform, where member interests do not collide, stays specific and directive. Practical implications. India can expect BRICS to deliver on institutional reform advocacy and technical cooperation while remaining unusable as an instrument of energy security, which matters given crude import dependence of 88.7 per cent in 2025-26. Policy weight should shift accordingly toward bilateral and sectoral channels. Limitations. The summit concluded two days before writing, so no peer-reviewed scholarship on it exists. The coding covers one issue area across two summits, which supports a descriptive claim rather than a causal one. Unique contribution. The paper supplies the first documented paragraph-level comparison of BRICS security language across the 2025 and 2026 declarations and proposes a reusable four-dimension coding scheme for measuring commitment strength in minilateral communiques.

title: SPY Realized Variance Forecasting with Rolling Elastic Net and Duan Smearing
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: SPY Realized Variance Forecasting with Rolling Elastic Net and Duan Smearing

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no competing financial or personal interests that could have influenced the work reported in this paper.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding.

detail.abstract: This study develops and evaluates a staged forecasting system for SPY realized variance from approximately 09:31 ET to the 16:00 ET close. The design begins with a 22-day rolling mean, HAR-RV, GARCH(1,1), and same-morning model-free implied variance (MFIV), then examines where the historical benchmarks fail across volatility, return-shock, intraday-path, and state-transition regimes. It next estimates log realized variance with rolling Elastic Net models and applies Duan's nonparametric smearing estimator when forecasts are retransformed to variance levels. Model development and validation use 1 January 2022 through 31 December 2023. The forecasting procedure is then fixed and evaluated sequentially over 667 trading days from 1 January 2024 through 28 August 2026; coefficients, selected support, penalty values, and smearing factors continue to update from information available before each forecast. HAR-RV significantly outperforms the rolling mean and GARCH, while raw MFIV significantly outperforms HAR-RV. The historical-feature Elastic Net reaches QLIKE 0.10645. Adding MFIV, implied-variance history, and option-surface features lowers validation QLIKE to 0.06478 and significantly improves both QLIKE and Spearman correlation relative to raw MFIV on all common dates. A residual HAR correction does not improve the base model. In the final window, the full Elastic Net IV model reaches QLIKE 0.11694 and significantly outperforms raw MFIV on QLIKE, but its rank correlation is statistically indistinguishable from both raw MFIV and a restricted MFIV-only Elastic Net. The evidence supports a calibration interpretation: Duan-smearing-adjusted log regression corrects the level of MFIV effectively, while the incremental contribution of the larger feature set is not statistically established in the final window.

title: Deference and Disengagement: Authoritarian Attitudes Trust among Trinidadian Youth
affiliations: University of Johannesburg

detail.title: Deference and Disengagement: Authoritarian Attitudes Trust among Trinidadian Youth

declarations.declarationOfInterest: No conflicts of interest to declare.
declarations.funderStatement: Unfunded research.

detail.abstract: Authoritarian attitudes are widely studied as a threat to democratic participation and institutional legitimacy, yet most of what is known comes from North American, European, and other majoritycontext populations. Drawing on an original 2019 survey of 1,210 young Trinidadians (aged 18-24, plus a small number of 25-year-olds) I ask who holds authoritarian attitudes, how those attitudes bear on political participation, and how they relate to trust in state institutions and satisfaction with government. Using a 14-item authoritarianism battery (α = .79) and OLS regression, I find authoritarianism significantly higher among men and less-educated respondents, with a significant negative effect on political participation net of media use and political engagement. Authoritarianism also significantly predicts higher institutional trust and higher life/government satisfaction net of controls, a pattern that runs counter to the erosion-of-trust relationship reported across most of the international literature. I read this pattern through Clive Thomas's account of the authoritarian state in peripheral societies and I show that the result survives re-estimation on a single common analytic sample, which rules out model-to-model differences in sample composition as the source. On that account deference and disengagement are complements, and this survey begins to supply the individuallevel evidence on legitimacy that Thomas's own treatment left thin.

title: Grid Bootstrap Inference for Threshold Quantile Regression

detail.title: Grid Bootstrap Inference for Threshold Quantile Regression

declarations.declarationOfInterest: None.
declarations.ethicsApproval: None.
declarations.funderStatement: None.

detail.abstract: We develop bootstrap-based inference for the threshold parameter in a threshold quantile regression (TQR) model. Extending the grid-bootstrap confidence interval of Hansen (1999) and the least-squares validity results of Hidalgo, Lee and Seo (2019) to the quantile regression setting, we prove that the rescaled bootstrap statistic converges to the correct limiting distribution under the null. The key theoretical ingredient is a maximal inequality for the quantile bootstrap process that exploits the boundedness of the quantile score function, which reduces the required moment condition from the eighth-order requirement of Hidalgo et al. (2019) to the simpler requirement of E| t | 4+η < ∞. We also establish consistency of the nonparametric estimator of the nuisance scale factor appearing in the rescaled likelihood-ratio statistic of Kuan et al. (2017). An extensive Monte Carlo study compares four nonparametric estimators of the nuisance parameter, Nadaraya-Watson, local linear, B-spline sieve, and k-nearest neighbours, against the asymptotic approximation across two data-generating processes, a heteroskedastic TQR model and a threshold quantile autoregressive model, three error distributions, three sample sizes, and five quantile levels. The study shows that the η2 rescaling is essential under heteroskedasticity since the correctly rescaled asymptotic interval is well calibrated at central quantiles and only moderately oversized at tail quantiles in small samples, while the grid bootstrap delivers its clearest improvements at the tail quantiles and small samples, where the asymptotic approximation is the weakest. Central quantiles remain the most demanding configuration for the bootstrap, because the nuisance parameter enters the procedure twice and is hardest to estimate at the median. Our implementation therefore pairs the quantile wild bootstrap of Feng, He and Hu (2011) with a smoothed conditional-scale construction that keeps the bootstrap error density well behaved. An application to the Debd/GDP for three countries concludes.

title: Associations Between Financial Education and Financial Behaviors Among U.S. Young Adults: A Secondary Analysis of the 2021 National Financial Capability Study
affiliations: Woodbridge High School

detail.title: Associations Between Financial Education and Financial Behaviors Among U.S. Young Adults: A Secondary Analysis of the 2021 National Financial Capability Study

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no competing financial or personal interests.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This study is a secondary analysis of de-identified, publicly available data from the FINRA Investor Education Foundation's 2021 National Financial Capability Study. No new data were collected from human participants, and institutional review board approval was not required.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no specific grant from any funding agency in the public, commercial, or not for profit sectors.

detail.abstract: Financial education, financial knowledge, and financial behavior are related but distinct constructs, and the 2021 National Financial Capability Study (NFCS) measures self-reported instructional exposure rather than impulsive spending. This secondary cross-sectional analysis examined 3,009 U.S. respondents aged 18-24. The primary comparison included 916 respondents who reported participating in financial education offered by a school, college, or workplace and 1,351 who reported that education was not offered; the remaining 742 were excluded. Weighted logistic and linear models used national post-stratification weights and adjusted for derived binary gender, race/ethnicity, education, employment, income, household structure, parental education, and large parental financial transfers. For the prespecified primary outcomes, reported financial education was not associated with lower spending above income (+2.7 percentage points, 95% CI [-2.2, 7.7], p = 0.275) or with a lower probability of carrying an interest-bearing credit-card balance (+4.8 pp, 95% CI [-1.7, 11.2], p = 0.151). Overdraft probability was higher in the primary comparison (+7.8 pp, p = 0.004) but attenuated when respondents who declined offered education were added to the comparison group (+3.4 pp, p = 0.185). Among secondary outcomes, financial education was associated with a 9.3 pp higher probability of holding a three-month emergency fund (95% CI [4.2, 14.5], p < 0.001), 0.34-point higher financial satisfaction on a 1-10 scale, and a 0.099-point higher score on a 0-3 knowledge scale. Because exposure and comparison groups were self-selected and the data were crosssectional, these estimates are associational; longitudinal or quasi-experimental designs are needed before drawing conclusions about effectiveness.

title: Quantile Process Inference and the Return-Volume Relation

detail.title: Quantile Process Inference and the Return-Volume Relation

declarations.declarationOfInterest: None!
declarations.ethicsApproval: None!
declarations.funderStatement: None!

detail.abstract: Chuang, Kuan and Lin (2009) document a symmetric V-shape in lagged volumes quantile effect on returns and a positive volatility effect, but lack formal statistical tests. Using the quantile regression process framework of Koenker and Xiao (2002), we identify four methodological gaps. First, we mathematically link the V-shape to volatility, providing formal V-shape tests and a joint Wald test for volatility. Second, we correct their family-wise error rate inflation by replacing their flawed multiple-testing approach with a single joint χ^2(9) test that properly accounts for the Brownian bridge covariance. Third, we apply the Khmaladze transformation to test whether volume reshapes the conditional distribution beyond a simple location-scale shift. Fourth, we generalize the V-shape template by allowing an unknown kink location and imposing monotonicity restrictions rather than exact linearity. Monte Carlo simulations confirm our joint test's superiority. Empirically, we find the NYSE volatility result is a false positive driven by multiple-testing inflation. While V-shapes exist across all indices, they exhibit strong asymmetry, correcting prior claims of symmetry. Extending the sample to 2024 reinforces these asymmetric findings, though strict goodness-of-fit tests ultimately reject all parametric templates, indicating deeper nonlinear structures in the true coefficient process.

title: Climate and Trade Policies in Energy Transition: Carbon Tariffs and Innovation

detail.title: Climate and Trade Policies in Energy Transition: Carbon Tariffs and Innovation

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no known competing financial interests or personal relationships that could have appeared to influence the work reported in this paper.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable. This study does not involve human participants or patients.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no specific grant from any funding agency in the public, commercial, or not-for-profit sectors.

detail.abstract: Trade policies affect innovation, but how carbon tariffs affect innovation and welfare remains much less understood. With carbon tariffs such as the EU Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism in place, it is crucial to understand their potential economic impacts, including how they interact with innovation in affecting technology levels. I develop a dynamic multi-country, multi-sector general equilibrium trade model with endogenous directed innovation in clean and dirty energies and non-energy goods, allowing for technology spillovers across sectors and countries. The quantitative simulation highlights that, without endogenous innovative responses, carbon tariffs shield domestic dirty production, increasing domestic emissions even if foreign emissions decline; they can also raise consumer prices and reduce real consumption and welfare. With directed innovation, however, carbon tariffs stimulate global green innovation and diffusion, accelerate the green energy transition, and enable welfare gains through substantial emission reductions and minimal consumption losses.

title: Masculinity Norms and the Far-right Backlash against Female Leadership
affiliations: Catholic University of the Sacred Heart of Milan, , University of Barcelona - Institut d'Economia de Barcelona (IEB),  and DISEIS, Faculty of Political and Social Sciences, Universita' Cattolica del Sacro Cuore

declarations.declarationOfInterest: Usual disclaimer applies.
declarations.funderStatement: Federico Franzoni acknowledges funding from European Union’s Marie Sk lodowska-Curie Actions Postdoctoral Fellowship for the project GEPU (Gender Equality and Populist Upsurge), Grant Agreement No. 101150168. Matteo Gamalerio acknowledges the research funds from project PID2024-160681NA-I00 (Ministerio de Ciencia, Innovaci´on y Universidades) and support by Baffi research center. Elisa Muscarella acknowledges support of the Joan Or´o FI predoctoral grant program of the Department of Research and Universities of the Government of Catalonia, co-financed by European Social Fund Plus (No. 2025 FI-1 00607).

detail.abstract: Does electing a female political leader fuel a far-right backlash? Using a regression discontinuity design on close mixed-gender mayoral races in Italian municipalities, we find that electing a female mayor raises the vote share of Lega - Italy's main populist radical right party - by 2.0 percentage points at the next general election, nearly doubling the average change. To investigate the mechanisms, we construct novel municipal-level indices of masculinity norms and gender norms, and show that the reaction is concentrated where dominance-oriented masculinity norms are stronger and is further amplified by local economic insecurity, while exhibiting no clear gradient along gender norms. This pattern is consistent with a status-threat mechanism. The results provide causal evidence that advances in women's political leadership generate a far-right electoral backlash, and identify dominance-oriented masculinity - rather than gender norms per se - as the cultural margin along which it operates.

title: The Human Genome Project: Craig Venter, Sydney Brenner and the Function-First Viewpoint
affiliations: Queen's University

detail.title: The Human Genome Project: Craig Venter, Sydney Brenner and the Function-First Viewpoint

declarations.declarationOfInterest: No interest declared
declarations.ethicsApproval: No patients involved, so no ethical concerns
declarations.funderStatement: Canadian Medical Research Council in the 1990s.

detail.abstract: The Human Genome Project (HGP) emerged in the 1990s after much dispute, with three levels of argument. First there were the later acclaimed "winners" for whom sequencing all human DNA was a primary goal. This mattered to them, whether or not genes occupied only a small part of our DNA. The best known of these was the recently deceased Craig Venter. Then there were those, such as Sydney Brenner, who thought that learning how to read DNA should have highest priority. Finally, there were researchers like me, who wished to first identify and target for sequencing those in the small genic part suspected of clinically important functions. Venter's choice of a human DNA fragment to test his methodology was a windfall both for Venter and for us. It overlapped a gene of clinical interest that we had identified a decade earlier after making a cDNA copy of the corresponding mRNA. This was used as an "expressed sequence tag" to identify its transcriptional source in a genome fragment library. By 1992 we already had a partial sequence and were poised for in-depth bioinformatic analysis when Venter published the complete sequence. This saved us time, so accelerating this and significant parallel studies.

detail.abstract: Understanding mortgage renegotiation requires distinguishing application history, eligibility across available programs, and delivered relief. Using 5.3 million servicing records from a distressed government-insured portfolio, I show that prior recorded application incompleteness is associated with a 2.19-percentage-point higher monthly probability of recorded foreclosure intent before April 2020, against a 2.05-point base rate. The estimate is 2.43 points using records of acknowledgement dispatch, 2.24 when observation begins after loss-mitigation activity, and 2.26 after conditioning on recorded borrower circumstances. Separately, 81.5 percent of loans ever denied on unemployment grounds were also recorded eligible for a retention option. Program denial rates and final outcomes cannot distinguish these configurations.

detail.abstract: Two companion papers argue that criminal-glorifying music recruits high-ability youth into organized crime by raising the community price of criminal prestige, and they test the claim on the educational composition of homicide victims. That evidence is open to an objection: the dead may differ from the living because of who is targeted rather than who is recruited. This paper tests the claim on a population selected by arrest rather than death. Using Mexico's 2021 national prison survey, we match offenders to the cultural salience of two narcocorrido traditions in the municipality and year of their crime, conditioning on the schooling of the local population. Among men sentenced for the business of a criminal organization, prestige-content salience predicts more educated entrants and violence-content salience predicts less educated entrants. Neither content predicts the schooling of men sentenced for armed offenses outside the core, for property crime, or for anything else. The two contents of the narcocorrido recruit for the two roles the organization needs to fill.

title: Anchors of Revival: Public Investment, Creative Clustering, and Transit Access in the Redevelopment of Deep Ellum, Dallas

detail.title: Anchors of Revival: Public Investment, Creative Clustering, and Transit Access in the Redevelopment of Deep Ellum, Dallas

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no conflict of interest.
declarations.funderStatement: No funding was received for this research.

detail.abstract: Deep Ellum, a historic neighborhood just east of downtown Dallas, has undergone a well-documented transformation over the past two decades: a formerly industrial and largely vacant district has become one of the region's most active mixed-use cultural and entertainment destinations, with certified taxable property value rising from roughly $189 million to nearly $1.5 billion since 2006. This paper examines the redevelopment of Deep Ellum as a case study in how cultural districts are built, drawing on the urban cultural economy literature, particularly Florida's creative-class thesis, Currid's account of cultural clustering as economic infrastructure, and Silver and Clark's "scenes" framework, alongside the public finance literature on tax increment financing (TIF) as a redevelopment tool. Using primary City of Dallas records documenting the Deep Ellum TIF District's formation, financing structure, and completed projects, together with the district's longer history as a Freedmen's Town, an early twentieth-century jazz and blues center, and a site of 1980s-1990s artist-led revival, the paper identifies several factors that appear to have jointly supported the district's turnaround: the opening of DART Green Line transit stations in 2009, targeted public infrastructure investment through the TIF district beginning in 2006, a pre-existing base of independent music venues and historic architecture that gave the district a distinctive identity, and sustained coordination through the Deep Ellum Public Improvement District. The paper closes by situating Deep Ellum within the broader literature on how successful cultural districts manage growth as they mature, and by highlighting recent City initiatives, including a 2024 set-aside of TIF revenue for housing stabilization, that reflect an evolving, proactive approach to sustaining the district's character alongside continued investment.

title: Assessing Adequacy Under VRE Forecast Uncertainty in Large-Scale Energy-System Planning

detail.title: Assessing Adequacy Under VRE Forecast Uncertainty in Large-Scale Energy-System Planning

detail.abstract: Long-term adequacy assessments commonly evaluate future expansion-plan scenarios under perfect-foresight operation. While such assessments capture the effects of realised weather variability, they do not explicitly test whether sufficient operational flexibility remains when schedules formed from imperfect variable renewable energy (VRE) forecasts encounter real-time generation. This distinction becomes increasingly important in future high-VRE systems, where operational decisions are made before actual VRE availability is known. This paper introduces the concept of forecast-error-driven adequacy assessment, develops a framework for its implementation and applies the framework to a large-scale energy-system model. The expansion-plan scenario is first evaluated through a multi-weather-year perfectforesight adequacy assessment. The same scenario is then reassessed under forecast-based operation, using lead-time-dependent and spatiotemporally correlated VRE forecast errors to link day-ahead scheduling, intraday gate-closure updates and real-time VRE availability. The resulting forecast-error-driven imbalances are compared with the modelled upward and downward flexibility from dispatchable generation, storage, VRE down-regulation and demand-side flexibility, with additional upward flexibility provided through imports across transmission corridors. The results show that an expansion-plan scenario assessed as adequate under multi-weatheryear perfect foresight can still experience non-negligible adequacy-relevant flexibility shortfalls when exposed to VRE forecast uncertainty. The magnitude of these shortfalls depends strongly on the extent of intraday adjustment, the availability of demand-side flexibility, and VRE participation in down-regulation. The findings highlight forecast uncertainty as a distinct source of operational flexibility stress that should be considered when interpreting the adequacy of future high-VRE energy systems.

title: Latent Resonance: Zero-Shot Autoencoder Inversion and Azimuthal Spectral Forensics for Diffusion Image Attribution

detail.abstract: Modern latent diffusion models (LDMs) synthesize photographic imagery with fidelity that evades human perception and frustrates conventional convolutional neural network classifiers. Existing forensic detectors rely predominantly on supervised binary classifiers that overfit to specific semantic domains or depend on closed API parameters. This paper introduces Latent Resonance, a zero-shot, white-box-free forensic framework grounded in the physical and architectural asymmetries between optical camera acquisition and latent autoencoder synthesis. By mapping candidate images through a deterministic autoencoder projection x = D(µ(E(x))) without noise injection (σ = 0), we isolate two distinct physical phenomena: spatial manifold resonance and transposed-convolution harmonic lattice spikes. Synthetic diffusion images originate directly from the decoder manifold D(z), yielding near-zero spatial reconstruction error (MSE = 0.000809 ± 0.000013, PSNR = 36.94 ± 0.07 dB). Conversely, authentic optical photographs suffer irreversible loss of physical sensor shot noise and Photo-Response Non-Uniformity (PRNU) across the 8× latent spatial bottleneck, producing significantly higher residual error (MSE = 0.001955 ± 0.000062, PSNR = 33.11 ± 0.14 dB, ∆ = +3.83 dB). In the frequency domain, azimuthally averaged 2D Fast Fourier Transform (2D-FFT) analysis reveals that diffusion residuals exhibit sharp periodic harmonic spikes (2.268× baseline) induced by transposed convolution upsampling strides, whereas authentic photos follow a smooth, continuous 1/f α power-law decay (1.141×). On clean native images, Latent Resonance achieves a verified 100.00% AUROC with zero false accusations. Under rigorous adversarial stress testing (lossy JPEG Q ∈ {95, 85, 75}, bicubic resampling 384 → 512, and Gaussian blur σ = 0.8), we demonstrate that combining spatial reconstruction margins with azimuthal spectral harmonics provides robust forensic discrimination where singledomain detectors collapse. All models, benchmark pipelines, and interactive inspection interfaces are released as a fully open-source reproducible artifact.

detail.abstract: Reference portfolios of listed equities and government bonds are increasingly used as benchmarks to evaluate the investment skill of institutional investors at the total portfolio level. We show that portfolio optimization away from the reference portfolio creates an inherent tension in this approach: the more a fund exploits sources of value-add, the more its portfolio deviates from the reference portfolio, generating tracking error that makes benchmark-relative performance a noisier measure of skill. Using a stylized fund calibrated to realistic levels of diversification, capital market assumptions, and manager and security selection, we find that more than 20 years of performance data are required to reliably distinguish skill from noise, far longer than the threeto five-year horizons typically used in practice. We propose approaches to quantify and interpret this uncertainty, isolate sources of value creation, and improve benchmark selection.

title:
Willingness Meets Capacity:
A Calibrated Sovereign Default Model for the Venezuelan Restructuring

detail.title:
Willingness Meets Capacity:
A Calibrated Sovereign Default Model for the Venezuelan Restructuring

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author is the founder and CEO of ARAP Inc., a sovereign debt restructuring analytics company whose platform includes the model and data infrastructure described in this paper. The quarterly GDP series, the calibrated default model and the debt-perimeter reconciliation were developed as part of the company's analytical work on the Venezuelan restructuring. No external funding was received for this research. The author has no financial position in Venezuelan sovereign or PDVSA bonds.

detail.abstract:
Debt-sustainability analysis asks how much a sovereign can pay. Strategic default mod-
els ask how much it will pay. We build a calibrated model of long-duration sovereign
debt for Venezuela and compute, for three macroeconomic scenarios and four debt
perimeters, the haircut required for the sovereign to be willing to re-enter markets and
stay current—and compare it with the capacity-based haircuts of the lead advisor’s
debt-sustainability analysis. Three results. First, willingness is uniformly stricter than
capacity: with preferences and income process both estimated on Venezuelan data, the
model requires a 66% haircut on the full claim universe under partial reform against a
capacity figure of 60%, and 39% against 32% under liberalisation—six to eight points
more in every reform scenario. Second, the gap widens under stagnation: the willing-
ness haircut is 78–89%, eight to nineteen points above the capacity figure of 70%, so a
settlement designed on capacity alone would be current on paper and in default in equi-
librium. Third, the income process behind these numbers is estimated, not assumed:
Venezuelan quarterly GDP follows a two-regime Markov-switching process—persistent
stagnation punctuated by short, violent collapses—whose parameters we cross-validate
across three independent implementations and two estimation paradigms, uncovering
along the way a local maximum that random-restart maximum likelihood reports as
the optimum. We also document that the standard best-response iteration for this
class of models does not converge in the deep-debt region of the state space under the
benchmark income process, show how a taste-shock smoothing scheme restores it, and
find that under the estimated Venezuelan process the iteration reaches a genuine fixed point. Finally, we reconcile the $234bn and $184bn figures for Venezuela’s external
claims to a zero residual, and show that the difference is definitional (accrued inter-
est), while the substantive uncertainty lies in the distinction between committed and
outstanding bilateral debt.

title: International Integrated Clearing and Settlement System (IICSS): A Multi-CBDC Distributed Ledger Architecture to Suppress Ex-Nihilo Credit Expansion

detail.abstract: The contemporary global monetary architecture suffers from two structural flaws: non-literal, messaging-based cross-border clearing and uncontrolled ex-nihilo credit expansion by commercial banks. This paper introduces the International Integrated Clearing and Settlement System (IICSS), a multi-CBDC distributed ledger technology (DLT) architecture designed to eliminate settlement risks and monetary inflation. By integrating Design Science Research (DSR), Agent-Based Computational Economics (ACE), and Financial Network Stress Testing (FNST), we evaluate the resilience of IICSS under extreme market shocks. The architecture enforces a 100% full-reserve constraint and deploys an Atomic Burn-and-Mint protocol via Hash Time-Locked Contracts (HTLC), replacing legacy Nostro-Vostro account messaging with instant value transfers. Monetary expansion is algorithmically bound 1:1 to verified real-sector output growth (Δ𝑀 = ∑ Δ 𝑌 𝑖) via tax invoice hashes and an All-Time High (ATH) historical margin rule. Computational stress testing demonstrates that IICSS achieves absolute immunity to bank run contagion (CI = 0.00) and tax fraud attacks (SLR → 0%) without causing liquidity shortages or depressing real economic growth.

detail.abstract: This chapter examines the presence of spatial dependencies of median house prices across local district authorities in England and enforces on how they are effected by integrating regulatory constraints into a spatial econometric framework. We employed a panel of 228 English districts from 1996Q1 to 2023Q4 and different forms of regulatory constraints normalized by the per square km of land area in a Spatial Durbin Model (SDM). Our results capture a significant presence of feedback loops through a high spatial regressive component (ρ) from which we inferred that districts are heavily connected and a price ripple from one districts would ripple across their neighbors. The indirect effects of regulatory constraints are almost 3 times that of the direct effect.

title: Too Young to Retire, Too Old to Work? Age and Gender Inequalities in Later-Life Employment in Ukraine

detail.title: Too Young to Retire, Too Old to Work? Age and Gender Inequalities in Later-Life Employment in Ukraine

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no known competing financial interests or personal relationships that could have appeared to influence the work reported in this paper.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no specific grant from any funding agency in the public, commercial, or not-for-profit sectors.

detail.abstract: Population ageing has increased interest in extending working lives, but the ability to remain employed at older ages may differ substantially across age groups and between women and men. This paper examines age and gender inequalities in later-life employment in Ukraine before the full-scale Russian invasion, focusing on employment, labour force participation, gender differences in average wages, and working conditions. Using aggregate official statistics from the State Statistics Service of Ukraine, the analysis documents employment and participation among women and men aged 50-59 and 60-70 over 2015-2021, examines unadjusted gender differences in nominal monthly wages among older employees in 2016 and 2020, and provides complementary industry-level evidence on harmful working conditions. The results reveal a pronounced age gradient in labour-market attachment. Employment and participation are substantially lower among individuals aged 60-70 than among those aged 50-59. At the same time, the gender employment gap among individuals aged 50-59 narrowed from 11.8 percentage points in 2015 to 3.8 percentage points in 2021, primarily because of rising female employment. Gender inequality nevertheless remains visible at older ages and in earnings. Women received lower average monthly wages than men in all three older age groups examined, although the relative gender wage gaps were smaller in 2020 than in 2016. Harmful working conditions also vary substantially across industries, with the highest average prevalence observed in transport and storage and construction. However, exploratory industry-level regressions provide no statistically robust evidence of a systematic association between harmful working conditions and aggregate employment. Overall, the findings point to substantial age differences, partial gender convergence, and persistent inequalities in later working life, while highlighting the importance of considering gender inequality and working conditions alongside policies aimed at extending working lives.

title: Aquascaping Games Need More Than Just Visual Appeal, They Need a Soul

detail.title: Aquascaping Games Need More Than Just Visual Appeal, They Need a Soul

declarations.declarationOfInterest: N/A
declarations.funderStatement: N/A

detail.abstract: Aquascaping is the craft of arranging aquatic plants, as well as rocks, stones, cavework, or driftwood, in an aesthetically pleasing manner within an aquarium-in effect, gardening under water. As a highly specialized real-world hobby, aquascaping involves expensive hardware, complex ecological maintenance, and a very high cost of trial and error. Digitizing and gamifying this hobby not only lowers the financial barrier and eliminates irreversible mistakes but also offers players a pure platform for creativity and visual enjoyment through time acceleration and game mechanics. This research report begins with a market survey of related games, analyzing the gameplay patterns and aesthetics of early and modern competitors to highlight their differences. Then it also deeply analyzes their commercial performance and the underlying reasons for their success or failure. This helps summarize the core system designs and technical challenges of next-generation aquascaping games, with a specific focus on how to integrate real-world experimental data of aquarium ecological cycles into the game. Finally, this report provides strategic design recommendations for the future development, including social, ethical, and accessibility considerations of such games.

title: Progressive or Degenerative Research Programs? A Lakatosian Reading of Insolvency Prediction and the ESG Agenda in Agricultural Cooperatives
affiliations: Pontifical Catholic University of Parana (PUCPR)

detail.title: Progressive or Degenerative Research Programs? A Lakatosian Reading of Insolvency Prediction and the ESG Agenda in Agricultural Cooperatives
detail.abstract: This essay examines, through the lens of Imre Lakatos's epistemology, whether research on insolvency prediction and on the relationship between ESG practices and financial performance constitutes, in the context of agricultural cooperatives, a progressive or a degenerative research program. Lakatos's methodology of scientific research programmes is presented in depth, with attention to the concepts of hard core, protective belt, negative and positive heuristics, and the criterion of empirical success based on the prediction of novel facts. These concepts are then applied to two empirical studies conducted by the author using data from Paraná agricultural cooperatives: a study on capital expenditure, asset growth, and insolvency risk, and a study on input exposure and economic-financial performance during the international fertilizer shock associated with the Russia-Ukraine War. It is argued that the results of these studies constitute empirical anomalies relevant to assessing the vitality of the dominant research program in this area. The essay concludes that the insolvency-prediction literature applied to cooperatives shows signs of stagnation when its financial hard core is not complemented by organizational variables, and that a more progressive research program would require explicitly incorporating adaptive capacity and governance as central, rather than auxiliary, variables.

title: An Ontology of Enduring Forms Organization as a Condition of Possibility, the Primary Field, Generative Morphogenesis, and Responsible Endurance

detail.title: An Ontology of Enduring Forms Organization as a Condition of Possibility, the Primary Field, Generative Morphogenesis, and Responsible Endurance

detail.abstract:
Symformism is developed as a relational and organizational ontology of enduring forms. Its central claim is that entities should not be treated as metaphysically primitive objects that subsequently enter into relations. Rather, relatively stable things emerge when processes of flow, constraint, memory, boundary formation, recurrence, and regulation become sufficiently organized to sustain a recognizable identity through change. The resulting unit is termed a symform: an organization whose continuity depends not on material immobility but on the maintenance, reconstruction, or transformation of constitutive relations.

The treatise extends this ontology beyond persistence itself. Once an organization becomes enduring, it can alter the conditions of possibility for subsequent states by changing pathways of access, transition costs, memory, constraints, and the reachability of future configurations. Organization therefore becomes not merely a description of what exists, but a causal condition of what can happen next.

To prevent the concept of symform from becoming indiscriminately applicable to every pattern, the work introduces an interventional criterion of organizational reality: a proposed organizational level earns independent explanatory weight only when counterfactual changes in relational organization, with relevant inventory approximately controlled, produce robust and practically meaningful differences in future behaviour, persistence, reconstruction, or reachability.

This framework is applied across physical systems, biology, cognition, institutions, technology, culture, and political organization. The treatise develops the concepts of dynamostasis, informational impedance, memory as altered accessibility, corrective reachability, cultural reachability, destructive persistence, and responsible endurance. It also distinguishes causal diagnosis from normative judgment: Symformist analysis produces multidimensional consequence profiles across scales and time horizons, while ethical evaluation requires separate and explicit commitments concerning autonomy, welfare, plurality, corrigibility, care, justice, and responsibility toward future generations.

At the physical frontier of the programme, the Primary Organizational Field and Dynamical Informational Field Theory (DIFT) are presented as bounded physical-ontological hypotheses and formal research laboratories rather than as established replacements for contemporary physics.

The resulting position combines processual realism, organizational causation, historical dependence, and multiscale diagnosis. Its guiding question is not merely what exists, but what must continue to happen for something to remain, what its persistence reorganizes around it, and which futures its continued existence makes more or less reachable.

title: Beyond Tariffs and Subsidies: Toward a New Framework for U.S. Industrial Policy -A Law and Development Analysis

detail.title: Beyond Tariffs and Subsidies: Toward a New Framework for U.S. Industrial Policy -A Law and Development Analysis

declarations.declarationOfInterest: N/A
declarations.funderStatement: The author acknowledges the support of the West Virginia University College of Law and the Arthur B. Hodges Summer Research Grant.

keywords: General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade (GATT)

detail.abstract:
The United States has returned to tariffs and subsidies with renewed force, seeking to rebuild domestic manufacturing, promote strategic industries, and counter geopolitical rivals such as China. This resurgence of industrial policy marks a sharp departure from the rule-based international trade order under the General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade and the World Trade Organization since 1947. Yet despite costly tariffs and hundreds of billions of dollars in subsidies, the economic results remain uncertain, while concerns over inflation, trade conflict, and market distortion continue to grow. Current debates in economics, politics, and trade law have focused largely on whether tariffs and subsidies are desirable. Far less attention has been paid to a more fundamental question: whether the United States possesses the legal and institutional capacity to implement industrial policy effectively. 

This Article addresses that question through the General Theory of Law and Development, a framework that examines how law, broader legal frameworks, and institutions shape economic and social transformation. It argues that contemporary U.S. industrial policy is structurally inadequate to achieve its stated objectives due to serious legal and institutional deficiencies undermining effective implementation, coordination, and policy coherence. These deficiencies also generate significant tensions with both domestic and international legal obligations, as illustrated by the Supreme Court's recent decision in Learning Resources, Inc. v. Trump. The Article develops foundational elements of a new legal and institutional framework for industrial promotion grounded in international collaboration, economic rationality, and institutional coordination.

title: Trade Secrets and Digital Twins: Tensions and Entitlements in Smart Factory and Smart City Contexts

detail.title: Trade Secrets and Digital Twins: Tensions and Entitlements in Smart Factory and Smart City Contexts

declarations.declarationOfInterest: No conflicting personal or financial relationships.
declarations.funderStatement: This work has been supported by the Carl Zeiss Foundation and the Kone Foundation, Finland “Long-term human rights risks of smart city technologies” project. Alina Wernick is a member of the Machine Learning Cluster of Excellence, EXC number 2064/1 – Project number 390727645.

detail.abstract:
Digital twins – virtual representations and simulations of physical objects, spaces and processes  – are expected to enhance efficiency and decision-making. Digital twins rely on the convergence of big data, Internet-of-Things, sensors, data analytics and artificial intelligence. They presuppose intimate, real-time tracking of the physical twin they represent, which may be a smart consumer product, a production unit, city infrastructure or a health status of a natural person. 

Where the owner of the physical twin is a company, the wide scope of organizational transparency and data collection necessary for the creation of an accurate digital twin may conflict with the practices required to maintain trade secrecy. Yet, digital twins may also support business and innovation processes and be commercially valuable due to their secrecy. In this chapter, I adopt a doctrinal perspective to assess the protectability of trade secrets in digital twins that are provided as a service. The analysis will apply the European law on trade secrets to two examples infrastructural digital twins: smart factory and an urban digital twin. 

The chapter uncovers that commissioner, and the provider of a digital twin may have overlapping interests to maintain the secrecy of the digital twin outputs. Under the EU trade secret doctrine, the provenance of data plays a little role in the allocation of a trade secret entitlement to the outputs generated from it. In the absence of contracting, the owner of a smart factory may not have a trade secrecy claim to the outputs of a digital twin, even though they represent commercially valuable information about their factory’s business operations. 

When deployed in an urban setting, digital twins may expose private businesses to reverse engineering of their trade secrets. However, municipalities may have a justifiable ground to integrate private data, including trade secrets, to urban digital twins in cases of public emergency. These problems are best addressed with a limited, well-drafted access right to the digital twin or its input or output data, that allows public sector bodies to fulfil their legitimate public duties while maintaining the confidentiality of trade secrets shared.

title: Investment Mandates and the Value of Distribution Timing in Currency Portfolios Choice

detail.abstract: The economic value of richer return forecasts depends on investors' ability to translate distributional information into portfolio decisions. We examine this relationship in currency markets, where observable interest-rate differentials discipline currency expected excess returns under the maintained no-predictability restriction for exchange-rate changes. We combine a multivariate model with time-varying volatility, skewness, and kurtosis with Bayesian online Sequential Monte Carlo estimation, incorporating parameter uncertainty directly into dynamic portfolio choice. In an out-of-sample exercise spanning 2006-2025, we consider a US investor allocating across nine major currencies. We compare mean-variance allocations with rules that additionally incorporate skewness and kurtosis under four mandates governing gross exposure, net directional exposure, and short selling. The economic value of distributional information depends critically on the investment mandate through which it can be implemented. The largest and most statistically robust gains arise when investors can adjust total exposure, while smaller and more heterogeneous gains remain under more restrictive mandates. The benchmark-relative results remain economically meaningful after proportional transaction costs, although their magnitude depends on the investment constraints and trading intensity.

detail.abstract: Land Use and Land Cover (LULC) constitute one of the most sensitive and observable expressions of the interaction between human activity and the physical environment, and its systematic monitoring are fundamental to sustainable regional planning. This study presents a spatio-temporal assessment of LULC change in Jammu district, Jammu and Kashmir, India, over the decade 2011-2021, using multi-temporal Landsat satellite imagery (Landsat 7 ETM+ for 2011 and Landsat 8 OLI/TIRS for 2021) obtained from the United States Geological Survey (USGS) Earth Explorer archive. Six thematic band composites were generated and classified through supervised Maximum Likelihood Classification (MLC) in a GIS environment into six land-cover classes-vegetation, agricultural land, built-up area, river bed, fallow land, and water bodies-following the USGS (Anderson et al., 1976) land-classification scheme. The classified layers were masked to the district boundary, and area statistics were compared between the two reference years to derive a quantitative change-detection matrix. The results reveal a pronounced landscape transformation: vegetation cover expanded from 40 per cent (940.38 km²) of the district in 2011 to 57 per cent (1,341.29 km²) in 2021, while agricultural land contracted sharply from 35 per cent (822.58 km²) to 17 per cent (401.70 km²) over the same period. Built-up area nearly doubled, rising from 5 per cent (121.38 km²) to 9 per cent (217.36 km²), reflecting rapid urban and infrastructural expansion around Jammu city and its peripheral towns, while fallow land declined from 15 per cent to 6 per cent and the riverbed class increased from 4 per cent to 10 per cent, most plausibly on account of hydrological and channel-migration processes along the Tawi and its tributaries. Water bodies remained a marginal but broadly stable 1 per cent of the district throughout. These findings depict a district in transition-from a predominantly agrarian, rural landscape toward one characterised by expanding green cover on the one hand and accelerating urbanisation on the other and they underscore the urgency of integrated, terrain-sensitive land-use planning that reconciles urban growth with the protection of agricultural and ecological resources. The study offers a replicable, GIS-based framework for monitoring land-use change in sub-Himalayan districts and provides an evidence base for future spatial planning in Jammu district and comparable regions of the northwestern Himalayan foothills.

detail.abstract: Traditional portfolio optimization models, such as the mean-variance framework developed by Markowitz, frequently rely on the assumption of multivariate normal return distributions. However, financial asset returns systematically exhibit fat tails, skewness, and time-varying volatility, rendering variance an inadequate metric for tail-risk management. This paper investigates the implementation of robust dynamic asset allocation strategies utilizing Conditional Value-at-Risk (CVaR) as a coherent downside risk measure under non-normal return distributions. By employing historical simulation and extreme value theory within a linear programming optimization structure, we construct dynamic portfolios that effectively safeguard against extreme market drawdowns. Empirical testing across multi-asset 1 benchmark universes reveals that CVaR-optimized portfolios achieve superior riskadjusted performance relative to traditional variance-minimized benchmarks during periods of market stress.

detail.abstract: This paper reviews the empirical finance literature on the effects of realized physical climate hazards on equity markets. Synthesizing evidence from 47 studies, it shows that climate-related events have significant impacts on stock returns, volatility, correlations, and, to a lesser extent, liquidity. From an investor perspective, negative effects dominate, particularly for extreme heat, tropical cyclones, droughts, and wildfires, but positive abnormal returns arise in specific sectors and contexts. The review documents substantial heterogeneity across hazards, regions, and firm characteristics, as well as a pronounced bias toward United States data and acute events. Finally, the paper discusses how these results on realized climate-related events can inform and enhance forward-looking frameworks for managing climate risks.

detail.abstract: Text watermarking is the latest method being widely discussed to make AI-generated writing detectable. Like other methods, it has technical limitations. However, we examine what even perfect detection would establish in academic publishing, focusing on authorship, intellectual credit, originality, responsibility, and provenance. We argue that the presence of AI-influenced text may correlate poorly with the degree and substance of human intellectual contribution.

detail.abstract: Retail markets rarely display a single observed price for an identical product. This paper develops a pricesystem framework in which the realized distribution of posted prices is treated not only as a description of dispersion but as a potential signal of the market-clearing process that repeatedly selects among feasible prices. Posted-price frequency is not demand. Instead, the paper proposes a conditional Marshallian interpretation: if prices that generate smaller excess-demand imbalances are more likely to persist or be selected again, then the modal posted price identifies a candidate focal clearing price, while the surrounding distribution reveals the width and direction of a revealed equilibrium region. The framework is evaluated with comparable first-half-of-month Mexican retail-price panels for January, February, and March 2026. The principal longitudinal sample contains 1,194 retailer-SKU systems across 12 FMCG categories and 150,728 posted-price observations in robust cells. Across the two monthly transitions, survival rises monotonically with prior price-point frequency: 35.9 percent of price points representing at most 2 percent of a system reappear in the next month, compared with 94.5 percent of price points representing more than 25 percent. The current modal price reappears in the next monthly window in 94.9 percent of transitions and remains the exact mode in 71.5 percent. The median within-system rank correlation of price-point frequencies is 0.823. When the mode changes, the sign of mass surrounding the current mode predicts the direction of the subsequent modal shift in 78.2 percent of cases, compared with a 55.7 percent majority-direction benchmark. These results do not prove market clearing without transaction quantities, but they establish dynamic restrictions consistent with a revealed-equilibrium interpretation and show that the current price distribution contains information about the subsequent pricing state.

detail.abstract:
Objective: The objective of this study is to investigate the effects of planned obsolescence, mainly in the competitive, environmental and consumerist areas. The study was carried out based on a careful analysis of specialized literature, including a brief comparative study of French and American Law. 

Theoretical Framework: The main references that support this study include the analysis of Law 12,529, the Brazilian Competition Law; the Consumer Protection Code and the Federal Constitution, and environmental standards from a national perspective. On the other hand, from the international analysis, the emphasis is on North American legislation and precedents of French Law, with the aim of establishing parameters in view of the challenges faced in Brazil. 

Method: The research adopts an exploratory descriptive approach, based on a bibliographic review and analysis of current legislation, using the hypothetical-deductive method to structure the investigation. 

Results and Discussion: Based on the theoretical framework and the legislative review, it was observed that the practice of planned obsolescence can represent an obstacle to fair competition, negatively impacting consumers and the environment. Furthermore, it is clear that there is a need to improve regulatory standards to curb this practice in Brazil. 

Research Implications: The results of this study can contribute to the improvement of legislation and public policies aimed at consumer protection and competition regulation, in addition to fostering academic and legal debate on planned obsolescence. 

Originality/Value: The originality of this research lies in the analysis of planned obsolescence from the perspective of Competition Law and Consumer Law, exploring its impact on the market and possible regulatory responses. The comparative study with other international legislation contributes to enriching the debate and to the formulation of more effective legislative proposals in Brazil.

detail.abstract: Logistics service providers increasingly invest in digital systems, sustainability initiatives, and security controls, yet conventional performance systems often evaluate these investments through short-term financial indicators alone. This paper develops and validates a dynamic balanced-scorecard model that links learning capability, digital capability, sustainability, security, internal process performance, customer outcomes, financial performance, and resilience. A reproducible synthetic panel of 48 logistics providers observed over 12 quarters produced 576 firm-quarter records. Firm fixed-effects models with quarter controls and cluster-robust standard errors were estimated using one-quarter lags. Lagged learning capability (beta=0.292), digital capability (beta=0.258), and security capability (beta=0.121) predicted internal process performance. Internal process performance predicted customer outcomes (beta=0.407), while customer outcomes, process performance, and security predicted financial performance. Learning and security were significant predictors of resilience; the direct lagged process coefficient was not. Model R-squared values ranged from 0.299 for resilience to 0.624 for financial performance. The study validates a temporal scorecard architecture but does not measure actual Egyptian logistics providers. It specifies how a future longitudinal study can connect capability investments to operational and financial realization. AI use disclosure. Generative AI tools assisted with language drafting, document formatting, and programming support. Farouk Eldakhlawy is responsible for independently verifying the research design, assumptions, code, numerical outputs, citations, figures, interpretations, and final text and for approving any version submitted or publicly posted.

The authors purposefully choose a Metropolis GZM, Poland (GZM), and Katowice Special Economic Zone (KSEZ). The importance of the high-tech sector in the GZM depends on the development of business in the region. Innovative specializations of cities located in the KSEZ were examined from the point of view of their perception by users of these new technologies, i.e., city residents.
