affiliations: Zhejiang University, Zhejiang University, Wenzhou Medical University - Oujiang Laboratory, Zhejiang University, Zhejiang University, Zhejiang University - Second Affiliated Hospital, Zhejiang University - School of Public Health and Zhejiang University - Eye Centre

detail.title: Multimodal Slit-Lamp Images For Cataract Evaluation: Development And Validation Of A Unified Deep-Learning Framework

declarations.declarationOfInterest: All authors have no conflicts of interest to disclose.
declarations.ethicsApproval: The Medical Ethical Committee of SAHZU approved this cross-sectional study (2023LSYD0456). Written informed consent was obtained from each participant.
declarations.funderStatement: This study was supported by grants from the Zhejiang Province Natural Science Foundation (LTGY24H120004), the National Natural Science Foundation of China (62476246), and the "Pioneer" and "Leading Goose" Research and Development Program of Zhejiang (2025C01132).

detail.abstract:
Background: To developed and validate a unified deep multimodal framework for comprehensive cataract evaluation from slit-lamp images (SLICE), integrating cortical, nuclear, and posterior subcapsular cataracts.

Methods: We conducted a development and validation study at a single center in Hangzhou, China, from June 2023 to February 2025.The dataset included 8,943 images from 2,981 eyes (67.4±20.0 years; 1,602 females and 1,379 males) for SLICE development and validation. All images were captured under mydriasis. Diffuse-illumination, slit-beam, and retroillumination imaging were used to assess cortical, nuclear, and posterior subcapsular cataracts, respectively. The proposed framework used a progressive two-phase strategy combining lesion-preserving data augmentation, dual-label soft supervision from two experienced ophthalmologists, and cross-modal feature fusion. 2,731 cases were assigned to the primary development cohort and 250 cases to an independent clinical validation cohort. Model performance was assessed using accuracy, weighted F1 score, mean absolute error (MAE), and quadratic weighted Cohen’s kappa (QWK).This study is registered with Chinese Clinical Trial Registry (ChiCTR), numbers ChiCTR2300071279.

Findings: The SLICE framework achieved accuracies of 81.97% for cortical, 80.33% for nuclear, and 77.87% for posterior subcapsular cataracts. Compared with other artificial intelligence models, the SLICE framework achieved an average accuracy of 80.05%, a weighted F1 score of 79.88%, QWK of 0.93, and a MAE of 0.24. Agreement was highest with the ophthalmologist who had 10 years of experience, with QWK values of 0.91, 0.92, and 0.63 for cortical, nuclear, and posterior subcapsular cataracts, and an overall cross-modal kappa of 0.82.

Interpretation: The proposed SLICE framework demonstrated clinically relevant performance for integrated patient-level cataract grading and may support more standardized cataract assessment.Funding: This study was supported by grants from the Zhejiang Province Natural Science Foundation (LTGY24H120004), the National Natural Science Foundation of China (62476246), and the "Pioneer" and "Leading Goose" Research and Development Program of Zhejiang (2025C01132).

detail.abstract: India's vision of becoming a high-income nation by 2047 is ambitious because of its significant forthcoming challenges to be faced to avoid the middle-income trap. In spite of its rapid growth during the last couple of decades, the economy has stagnated in its contribution to the agricultural and service sectors, and thus is unable to transition to a more advanced and diversified nation. Amid global challenges, India's robust recovery after the financial and the COVID-19-led crisis instils optimism, with forecasts envisioning a transition to high-income status, surpassing 30 trillion USD GDP. However, the vision of a ‘Viksit Bharat’ (developed India) by 2047, marking 100 years of independence, would face serious challenges. For India, the road ahead is fraught with structural issues, climate risks, and socio-economic inequalities that would constrain achieving long-term prosperity.

title: TAPER Study Qualitative Analysis: How Women Balance Decision-making About Hormone Replacement Therapy (HRT) (dis)continuation ​
affiliations: University of Birmingham - Institute of Applied Health Research, University of Birmingham, Black Women in Menopause, Cysters and University of Birmingham

detail.title: TAPER Study Qualitative Analysis: How Women Balance Decision-making About Hormone Replacement Therapy (HRT) (dis)continuation ​

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors declare they have no completing or conflicting interests
declarations.ethicsApproval: The TAPER Study was sponsored by University of Birmingham (RG25-010) and received a favourable ethical opinion from the North-west-Liverpool central Research Ethics Committee 25/NW/0168 on 18th June 2025 (IRAS ID: 337337). Participants provided informed consent,
declarations.funderStatement: This study/project is funded by an NIHR Advanced fellowship award (NIHR304353).

detail.abstract:
Background: The TAPER Study aims to explore what matters most to women and healthcare professionals (HCPs) when women consider stopping or restarting hormone replacement therapy (HRT). There is limited evidence to help women and their HCPs decide when and how to stop HRT. Stopping HRT often leads to the recurrence of menopausal symptoms which can negatively affect quality of life.  Some women choose to restart HRT which can lead to a stop-restart cycle. This cycle may adversely affect women and increase healthcare use and costs.

Methods: An exploratory qualitative study was conducted using semi-structured interviews.  Twenty-six women aged 50-67 years were recruited through GP surgeries serving diverse populations and targeted social media adverts shared by community organisations. All interviews were all conducted remotely.  Participants identified as Asian (n=4), Black (n=1) Mixed ethnicity (n=1) or white (n=20). Following informed consent, interviews were audio-recorded, transcribed and anonymised, and uploaded to NVivo 14 to support data management and analysis.  Transcripts were analysed using codebook thematic analysis, using an iterative deductive-inductive approach in which the discussion guide was used to create the initial deductive coding template.

Findings: Women made decisions to start, continue, stop, and/or restart HRT at different points, based on wider influences and assessments of their personal risk. These influences and risk assessments frequently intersected and included fear of, or actual, symptom recurrence; family experiences of menopause; perceived breast cancer risk; time spent using HRT; and considerations about whether they were post-menopausal. Women described uncertainty about the impact of stopping HRT and wanted more information about the likelihood and management of symptom recurrence following discontinuation.

Interpretation: Women’s decision-making around HRT discontinuation and restarting was influenced by multiple, intersecting factors. Individualised support and clear information were needed to enable informed decision making and support women choosing to discontinue HRT.

detail.abstract:
This book examines the transformative changes in international corporate taxation from 2008 to 2021, culminating in the landmark October 2021 Agreement that fundamentally altered multinational business taxation.

The study analyses how the 2008 Financial Crisis and 2020 COVID-19 pandemic catalysed reform through G-20 and OECD initiatives, resulting in a two-pillar framework with conditional mismatch rules and a 15% minimum Effective Corporate Tax Rate applied country-by-country.

Through empirical, comparative, and meta-historical analysis, the author reveals the decisive influence of the Transnational Tax Policy Community (TTPC) as agenda-setter, adviser, and gatekeeper. Despite the TTPC’s significant role, the research demonstrates that domestic politics substantially impact implementation and enforcement outcomes.

The work introduces a Dynamic Model of Corporate Tax Governance that not only explains recent revolutionary changes but also predicts future developments in global tax governance, illuminating the ongoing tension between multilateral cooperation and state sovereignty in international taxation.

detail.abstract: Food costs in India have substantially increased from 2022 to 2025 mainly due to a mix of various global supply chain disruptions, climate change impacts, regional agricultural deficits, and inflationary pressures that are mostly attributable to the COVID-19 pandemic and the Russia-Ukraine war (RBI). Such factors have brought about continuous rises to the prices of basic goods such as grains, legumes, and vegetables, which in turn have changed to a large extent the purchasing behaviours of low-income families. The issue, however, is concentrated in Rajasthan to a great extent, where a large number of BPL families that live below the poverty line are engaged in spending more than 60% of their scanty income on food only (NSSO). Such price hikes make it necessary for poor families to buy cheaper, less nutritious versions of essential staples, thus, their chances of suffering from malnutrition go up (World Bank).

detail.title: Consensus Amplifies Dot Plot Surprises: Ex Ante Dispersion and Treasury Yield Responses to the SEP

detail.abstract: The market impact of the Federal Reserve's dot plot depends on the expectations formed before its release. Using 43 Summary of Economic Projections meetings from September 2015 through June 2026, this paper measures surprises in the projected federal funds rate path relative to the Federal Reserve Bank of New York's pre-meeting surveys and combines them with high-frequency Treasury yield changes. Unconditionally, a 25-basis-point upward path surprise is associated with yield increases of about 4.4, 3.7, and 1.6 basis points at the two-, five-, and ten-year maturities, none of which is estimated precisely. Conditioning on the pre-meeting expectation distribution changes this picture. The same path surprise produces a substantially larger yield adjustment when pre-meeting expectations are concentrated: the interaction between the path surprise and survey dispersion is negative at all three maturities, with estimates of-424,-487, and-360 basis points per percentage point squared after controlling for revisions to inflation, unemployment, and growth projections. Evaluated at the tenth percentile of dispersion, a 25-basis-point surprise moves the twoyear yield by 18.6 basis points; at the ninetieth percentile the response is indistinguishable from zero. The interaction is negative in all 43 leave-one-meeting-out estimates and improves held-out predictive accuracy at the five-and ten-year maturities. Market disagreement, not dispersion across FOMC participants' published rate projections, generates this attenuation; the dot-dispersion interaction is positive rather than negative and is at most marginal. The effect appears in the initial release window, continues through the press conference, and accumulates over the full SEP event. Cross-panel construction and a reliability-based assessment indicate that survey measurement error attenuates rather than manufactures the result. Pre-meeting consensus is therefore a central determinant of dot plot transmission: the projected path matters not only through how far it moves, but also through how firmly the market had converged before publication.

title: Costing the transition to absolute sustainability: Allocating environmental and social transformation costs to product systems
affiliations: and Saarland University

detail.title: Costing the transition to absolute sustainability: Allocating environmental and social transformation costs to product systems

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors declare that they have no known competing financial interests or personal relationships that could have appeared to influence the work reported in this paper.
declarations.funderStatement: This research did not receive any specific grant from funding agencies in the public, commercial, or not-for-profit sectors. It was carried out as part of the authors' institutional research activities at the Institute of Product Engineering, Saarland University.

detail.abstract: Absolute sustainability assessment enables the evaluation of product systems in relation to Earth's carrying capacities and minimum social thresholds, supporting targeted mitigation towards a sufficient state. Yet foreground engineering has limited leverage over impacts arising in supply chains and background systems, often leaving residual gaps that require systemic transformation. For this purpose, the present work introduces absolute sustainability cost assessment (ASCA) to determine the expenditure required to address these residual gaps towards achieving absolute sustainability. ASCA extends life cycle costing by allocating the prospective implementation costs of background system transformation to the functional unit of a product system. Ten qualification criteria for such measures are proposed, together with a catalogue of 136 candidates across sixteen environmental impact categories and eleven social thresholds. Applied to an electric bicycle, ASCA derives costs for five of nine residual environmental gaps with established characterization factors at 1.56E-03 to 4.36E-03 USD/pkm, a surcharge of 0.70-1.97 % on conventional life cycle costs of 0.2218 USD/pkm. If additional conversion assumptions are permitted, coverage rises to eight of nine environmental categories at 4.32E-03 to 8.21E-03 USD/pkm and includes an estimate of 1.38E-04 to 6.31E-03 USD/pkm for addressing all eleven social risk gaps, resulting in a total premium of 2.01-6.55%. ASCA thus reframes the internalization of externalities from pricing damages to financing systemic transformation and operationally introduces background impact mitigation into engineering decisions.

detail.abstract: Waves of products liability litigation against Meta, TikTok, Snap, and YouTube are forcing courts to decide whether designed features are protected "publishing" functions under Section 230 of the Communications Decency Act or product-design choices subject to tort law. In the 2026 case of K.G.M. v. Meta Platforms, Inc., for example, a California jury found Meta liable under tort for harms associated with a minor's compulsive use of Instagram, signaling a willingness to evaluate social media platforms as products with designed features that can contribute to foreseeable harms. Similar questions about the line between product design and protected expression have likewise emerged in litigation involving artificial intelligence systems. In Garcia v. Character Technologies, Inc. (2024), a mother alleged that Character.AI's chatbot product was designed in ways that contributed to her child's harm, while Character.AI argued that its conversational outputs constituted protected speech under the First Amendment. This article presents a history of social and networked software products, with a particular focus on social media, to demonstrate how contemporary social media and AI systems are engineered modularly such that "speech" components, and "product" components, are distinct. In sum, this article argues that product design elements are analytically and legally unique from the content they transmit and should thus be evaluated separately from questions of protected expression.

detail.abstract: AI is transforming one of the oldest and most consequential decisions in business. The opportunity is not simply to automate pricing, but to make it more intelligent, adaptive, and personalized. AI allows companies to analyze more data, experiment with prices at scale, and adjust decisions dynamically, while generative AI makes sophisticated pricing capabilities accessible through natural language. Yet these advances also create new challenges. Pricing recommendations can depend heavily on the data, model, and prompts, and the most profitable price may not always be the right one when fairness, trust, and regulation are considered. Importantly, human judgment remains essential. Drawing on my recent book, Pricing in the Age of AI, as well as research and real-world examples, this article examines how AI is reshaping pricing and offers five rules to help executives use it effectively and responsibly: experiment continuously, use AI as a copilot, treat the prompt as part of the pricing system, keep humans accountable, and optimize for trust, not just profit.

detail.abstract: In the US federal system, the federal government provides substantial fiscal support to state and local governments. In this paper, we describe how the landscape of intergovernmental grants, which exceeded $1.2 trillion in 2025, evolved during and in the wake of the COVID-19 pandemic. We provide short-run evidence on how state and local government budgets have adapted as pandemic-era fiscal supports wound down. We further emphasize the pressures state and local budgets will face as several provisions of the One Big Beautiful Bill Act (OBBBA), which are intended to restrain intergovernmental grants, go into effect over the coming years.

detail.abstract: Population ageing raises fiscal pressure, but its healthcare consequences depend on whether longer lives are also healthier. Using Spain as a case study, this paper combines a retrospective age-profile counterfactual with official long-term fiscal benchmarks to quantify the healthcare dividend of healthy ageing and assess its significance relative to pensions and long-term care (LTC). Applying fixed 2019 age-specific healthcare expenditure profiles to the 2000 and 2025 population structures implies a 14.1% increase in weighted healthcare expenditure due solely to demographic composition. Allowing 50% of the observed gain in life expectancy at age 65 to shift expenditure profiles towards older ages reduces the increase to 11.9%; full compression reduces it to 9.7%. In fiscal sensitivity analysis, healthcare savings of 0.1-0.3 percentage points of GDP offset only about 3-10% of projected pension pressure. Projected LTC expenditure rises by about 0.6 percentage points of GDP to 2050, further limiting the aggregate fiscal offset. The results suggest that healthy ageing generates meaningful healthcare savings, but only modestly reduces the overall fiscal cost of longer lives. The paper distinguishes the demographic cost of ageing from the expansion of the welfare frontier through broader coverage, formalisation and intensity of care.

detail.abstract: We reveal an economic identity of the modeling of an elementary index or inflation determined by a particular good or service and of a security's gross return traded at the exchange. We highlight that to be economically valid, a month-to-month elementary index should be calculated as the ratio of the prices adjusted to the same time by its elementary inflation before performing the price averaging. This is overlooked by the current theory and practice. We partially fill this flaw and derive the equation for the adjusted elementary inflation and obtain its successive approximations determined by the prices of trades adjusted by the elementary inflation to same time. The accuracy of these approximations is determined by the usage of unadjusted mean prices during the past periods. We use the likeness of the elementary index and security's gross return and introduce random elementary inflation and its market-based variance, which accounts for the impact of random trade volumes on the variance of inflation. We propose the well-known Sharpe (1966) Ratio as a measure of the uncertainty of the current and predicted assessments of the elementary inflation. To be economically reasonable, any forecast of elementary inflation should be accompanied by the forecast of its variance.

detail.abstract: We specify a source-preserving multicriteria decision policy that distinguishes internally conflicting sources, opposed sources, insufficient evidence and directional decidability before ranking. Criterion aggregation takes place within each source; aggregation across sources is postponed until the decision to rank. Formal results establish the policy’s partition, conflict persistence, symmetry behaviour and stability away from threshold boundaries. A reproducible audit compares forced mean decisions, mean-level withholding and two source-level coalition rules on identical panels. Stipulated instrument responses expose conflicts diluted by criterion aggregation. Simulated coherent, sparse, opposed and internally conflicting panels show that withholding can prevent unsupported decisions but can also incur avoidable abstention under a stipulated latent direction. Coverage and conditional error are therefore reported jointly, together with loss under declared abstention costs. These results describe the policy and its trade-offs; they do not establish empirical superiority. A provenance-based protocol specifies the independent outcomes needed for real-panel evaluation.

title: "Remedial Closure" of the Strait of Hormuz; Dialectic of Legality and Legitimacy

detail.abstract: This research develops an innovative framework for legal assessment of the closure or restriction of the Strait of Hormuz during the situation that threatens a coastal state's survival. The central analysis is structured around four dualistic 2 questions which ask how "internationally legal", how "internationally legitimate", how "legally legitimate" and how "legitimately legal" such a closure would be. The hypothesis of this article is that in the exceptional circumstance of self-defense where state survival is at stake, legitimacy may, under strict conditions, justify a departure from strict positivist legality, giving rise to a new conceptual framework rather than a rule-based exception. Methodologically, the article employs a dialectical approach that moves from the positivist prohibition as the thesis through a legitimacy-based critique as the antithesis to a synthetic resolution. This dialectical movement is complemented by reasoning by analogy in particular from the International Court of Justice's Nuclear Weapons and Kosovo advisory opinions. The central finding is that a strict positivist reading of the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS) and customary international law provides no explicit authorization for closure and leaves the victim state helpless. The article's main hypothesis is that in appearing an existential threat, legitimacy may override mere legality, giving rise to a new legal institution. To operationalize this hypothesis, the article proposes the doctrine of remedial closure as an emergency mechanism grounded in the inherent right of self-defense and strictly conditioned on legal tests. The theoretical results demonstrate that legality and legitimacy are not binary opposites but dialectical partners within a living legal order. The article concludes that even though the closure of the Strait of Hormuz has very little support for legal acceptance under a purely positivist reading, legitimately it can be considered authorized under a reasoned and dialectical interpretation of international law, provided all cumulative requirements are satisfied.

detail.abstract: Variable annuities (VAs) have been among the most prevalent equity-linked insurance products in the U.S. over the past two decades. Despite their insurance nature, VA guarantees are predominantly valued using risk-neutral pricing methods. Using empirical data on U.S. VA contracts with 10-year Guaranteed Minimum Maturity Benefit riders, we demonstrate that risk-neutral pricing systematically overestimates insurance fees relative to observed market fees and cannot explain the existence of many contracts without surrender penalties. Motivated by these mismatches, we develop a risk-sharing pricing framework in which a profit-maximizing insurer and a risk-averse policyholder interact through a Stackelberg game. Beyond reconciling observed contract features and pricing outcomes, the framework provides a characterization of viable VA markets by jointly determining policyholder demand, surrender behavior, and insurer pricing. In particular, it identifies the policyholder characteristics and market environments under which VAs are preferred to risk-free assets and uninsured equity investments and can be profitably supplied by insurers. These findings offer useful implications for insurers in designing and pricing VA products and for broker-dealers in making recommendations consistent with the principles underlying the SEC's Regulation Best Interest, which has applied to broker-dealers since June 2020. Our findings highlight the central role of risk sharing in the valuation of VA guarantees and provide an economic foundation for understanding the pricing, design, and sustainability of VA markets.

detail.abstract: Generative AI music has moved from narrow task assistance to full-song creation and platform formation. This case study examines Suno’s evolution from a prompt-to-song generator into a vertically expanding ecosystem encompassing professional production, artist development, licensed repertoire, identity and consent controls, distribution governance, and artist–fan participation. It applies an evolutionary framework—variation, inheritance and selection—to company announcements, rights-holder releases, court and government materials, platform policies and trade reporting available through September 5, 2026. The analysis finds that competition is shifting from model quality toward ecosystem fitness; rights are becoming product architecture; human agency is becoming a premium source of value; and the most plausible market structure is a federated hybrid ecosystem rather than winner-take-all consolidation. Suno’s principal advantages are scale, subscription revenue, capital capacity, product depth and partnership momentum. Its principal constraints remain unresolved questions concerning training authorization, allegedly infringing outputs, artist identity and publicity rights, distribution integrity and creator trust. New actions involving individual musicians, SOCAN, and Gerencia 360 illustrate how legal pressure now spans identity, output, streaming, catalog and data-acquisition issues. The case study concludes that durable advantage will accrue to the platform—or network of platforms—that can make musical abundance trustworthy through authorized inputs, identity controls, auditable human contribution, interoperable provenance (sourcing), professional finishing and accountable delivery.

detail.abstract: Why did probabilistic optimization come to monopolize AI development while symbolic, causal, and interpretable alternatives were marginalized? Moving beyond model-centric accounts of AI alignment, this article grounds model failures in the political economy of platform infrastructure. We trace a post-2008 convergence in which financial valuation and risk-management rationalities migrated into digital advertising. Real-time bidding platforms institutionalized this transfer, pricing attention at millisecond speeds and subordinating explanation to execution velocity. Within this regime, we reframe two core phenomena, hallucination functions as synthetic epistemic liquidity which is fluent text generated to maintain transactional flow when empirical grounding is absent; Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF) operates as a liquidity-management tool that masks model fragility by externalizing volatility onto precarious human annotators. The result is an epistemic liquidity crisis: systems overproduce fluent, confidence-inducing output while their capacity to remain grounded in shared reality fails to keep pace. Ultimately, alignment is a struggle over the political economy of knowledge production. Technical fixes confined to the model layer merely polish the surface, leaving the structural incentives that generate misalignment fully intact.

title: The Experience Gap: A Conceptual Framework for Understanding the Disconnect Between Work Design and Lived Employee Experience

detail.title: The Experience Gap: A Conceptual Framework for Understanding the Disconnect Between Work Design and Lived Employee Experience

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author is the founder and CEO of Sovera, a consultancy that advises organizations on workplace design, workforce transformation, employee experience of workplaces, digital transformation and the human experience of organizational change, including topics addressed in this paper. detail.abstract:
Organizations devote substantial resources to designing policies, benefits, technologies, managerial practices, and workplace structures intended to improve employee well-being, flexibility, engagement, and performance. The presence of organizational support, however, does not establish that employees experience that support as effective. This paper introduces the Experience Gap, defined as the divergence between the conditions of work an organization intends, communicates, or formally provides and the conditions employees actually experience.

The construct is developed from a sequential multimethod study of 35 full-time working parents in medium and large organizations who experienced workplace model shifts following March 2020. The study found that supportive management, flexible work arrangements, and trust-based cultures were perceived as especially important, while every organizational support category assessed exhibited a positive importance-effectiveness gap. Qualitative findings further demonstrated distinctions between nominal and functional resources, between formal policy and cultural permission, and between work arrangements employees could meaningfully shape and those controlled primarily by organizational demands.

Working parents serve here as a theoretically useful population for examining work design, and no claim is made that their experience is uniform across the workforce. Because caregiving intensifies the convergence of professional, relational, temporal, and logistical demands, working parents can expose structural contradictions that may remain less visible for employees with greater capacity to absorb them. The original study identified working parents as a potentially sensitive indicator of broader organizational dysfunction while calling for extension to other caregiving and employee populations.

Integrating job demands-resources theory, role theory, boundary theory, and organizational-support research, this paper advances seven propositions concerning the conditions under which an Experience Gap develops and its potential consequences. The framework shifts attention from the presence of organizational provisions to their function in lived experience and proposes that work design should ultimately be evaluated by whether employees can translate organizational resources into sustainable capacity for contribution and well-being.

detail.abstract: Over the past two decades, massive enterprise capital investments in information technology and digital transformation have failed to universally drive proportional increases in Return on Invested Capital (ROIC), resurrecting the "Productivity Paradox" in the era of industrial intelligence. Bridging Value Chain Management and Systems Science, this paper identifies the root cause as a structural mismatch in underlying paradigms: conventional enterprise architecture and management models assume "Independent and Identically Distributed (IID)" weak coupling among functional modules, whereas real-world discrete manufacturing value networks are intrinsically Non-IID, high-dimensional, strongly-coupled Open Complex Giant Systems (OCGS). Grounded in systems science first principles, we establish "Value Chain Physics" as the concrete domain projection of systems science in physical enterprise networks. We construct a Systemically Complete and Irreducible (SCI) five-dimensional topological manifold ℳ(𝑡) = ⟨𝒩, 𝒯, 𝒞, 𝒙(𝑡), Δ𝒙(𝑡)⟩. The nonorthogonal interference across these five dimensions is proven to be the physical origin of control vector "Vector Cancellation" under multi-departmental local optimization, generating internal dissipative heat Δ𝑊 heat = ∑ ∥ 𝑉 𝑖 ∥-∥ ∑𝑉 𝑖 ∥> 0 that erodes ROIC. Furthermore, we propose a 5D Double-Helix Architecture intertwining a Holographic Data Model (Left Helix) and a Dynamic Evolution Algorithm (Right Helix). The Prior Partition Operator 𝚷 projects the factorial 𝒪(𝑁!) search space onto a bounded feasible space Ω feasible via Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG) topological ordering. The Rigid Manifold Operator 𝚷 ⊥ strips normal non-orthogonal internal friction degrees of freedom (𝑥 ⊥ (𝑡) → 0), reducing search complexity to polynomial scale 𝒪(𝑁log𝑁) (with an empirical upper bound of 𝒪(𝑁log𝑁) for bounded treewidth networks). In the continuous Banach space (Ω, ∥⋅∥ 2), we prove the unique existence and exponential convergence of a closed-loop steady state 𝑥 * via the Banach Contraction Mapping Theorem, guarded by a Compact Support Projection Operator 𝑬 supp that truncates heavy-tailed residual distributions to mitigate Goodhart's Law collapse. Finally, under explicit mathematical conditions (𝚷 partitioning, 𝚷 ⊥ constraints, spectral radius 𝜌(𝑨) < 1, and human second-order meta-introspection 𝚽), we provide formal mathematical proofs for the necessary and sufficient conditions of Qian Xuesen's three core OCGS principles (Overall Design Department, Hall of Workshop for Decision Support, and Human-Machine Integration with Human-in-the-Lead). Empirical verification across a 10-year longitudinal field deployment (2015-2024) across Lenovo's global manufacturing network (including the WEF Lighthouse Factory in Hefei) and third-party audited financial metrics confirms that closed-loop autonomous decision-making ("human-out-of-the-loop" execution) dramatically reduces stoppage frequencies, releases RMB 3.5+ billion in NWC, and drives sustained ROIC elevation.

detail.abstract:
What if crisis is not the end of a generational cycle, but the moment society becomes capable of recognizing what it has been repeating? The Fifth Turning: From Revelation to Resolution proposes a population-health theory of conscious institutional reconstruction. It asks one central question: What conditions will one generation transmit to the next?

The theory argues that generations do not begin at zero. They inherit institutions, policies, economic conditions, historical trauma, cultural memory, health exposures, data systems, and technologies that can reproduce inequality across generations. The Fifth Turning proposes five processes for interrupting that transmission: Recognition, Reckoning, Interruption, Reconstruction, and Transmission.

The framework connects population health, structural racism, social determinants of health, institutional persistence, cultural memory, artificial intelligence, data equity, and community-based intervention. It introduces the Fifth Turning Resolution Standard, Truth Data Standard, Truth-Teller Generation, and eight falsifiable propositions for future empirical testing.

The central argument is simple: crisis alone does not create transformation. Transformation begins when societies recognize what they inherited, interrupt the mechanisms reproducing harm, reconstruct the institutions carrying those conditions forward, measure whether conditions changed, and deliberately transmit something different.

title: When Does LLM-Extracted Central Bank Sentiment Add Value? A Fragility Analysis of Sentiment-Tilted CVaR Portfolios in FX Markets

detail.abstract: This paper stress-tests a common claim in the emerging LLM-for-finance literature: that LLM-extracted sentiment can improve risk-based portfolio optimization. Using the full text of 45 FOMC statements (January 2021-July 2026), Google's Gemini 2.5 Flash model, IG Markets broker-executable daily prices, and official central-bank policy rates for carry, we construct a sentiment-tilted Conditional Value-at-Risk (CVaR) strategy on six major USD currency pairs and subject it to a battery of robustness checks rarely applied jointly in this literature: a formal Sharpe-ratio equality test, a 500-permutation placebo test, eventlevel clustered inference with block and stationary bootstrap confidence intervals, a nested walk-forward procedure for selecting the tilt-strength parameter without look-ahead, a Minimum-Variance benchmark, a Loughran-McDonald dictionary comparison, pair-specific transaction-cost and FOMC-announcementwindow stress tests, and two stability probes-repeated LLM queries and substitution of three reproducible alternative model families (Llama 3.1 8B, GPT-OSS 120B, Qwen 3.6 27B). The central finding is fragility, not confirmation. The main specification shows a higher point-estimate Sharpe ratio (0.398 to 0.609) and Sortino ratio (0.494 to 0.877) than a sentiment-free baseline, but a Jobson-Korkie/Memmel test does not reject equal Sharpe ratios (p = 0.699; 95% CI for the difference: [-0.861, 1.285]), and the genuine signal falls at only the 78th percentile of the 500-permutation placebo null. Every stability probe degrades, reverses, or fails to confirm the result: re-running the backtest with the 10repetition mean polarity score in place of the single-pass score all but eliminates the Sharpe ratio (-0.001, against individual single-repetition Sharpe ratios ranging from 0.081 to 0.628) despite 0.979 correlation with the single-pass score; of three reproducible alternative model families, Llama 3.1 8B raises the Sharpe ratio to 1.063 while GPT-OSS 120B and Qwen 3.6 27B lower it to 0.300 and 0.157, and none is statistically distinguishable from the Baseline (Memmel p = 0.217, 0.861, and 0.669 respectively). A fourth model, Llama 3.3 70B, was deprecated by its provider before this specification was finalized and could not be reevaluated; its earlier point estimate (Sharpe = 0.153) is reported for completeness only. A look-ahead-free procedure for the tilt-strength parameter λ selects a positive tilt in 30 of 58 periods, yet the resulting out-ofsample Sharpe ratio (0.393) is statistically indistinguishable from a fixed no-tilt policy. Two comparisons complicate a purely negative reading, though not in the direction a diversification story would predict. A Minimum-Variance benchmark with no sentiment achieves a Sharpe ratio (0.336) below both the Baseline and the LLM-tilted strategy, so generic risk-minimization alone does not explain the apparent gain over the naive Baseline; the source of the Baseline's own advantage over pure varianceminimization is a question we do not resolve here. A Loughran-McDonald dictionary signal underperforms the baseline and turns the strategy's realized Sharpe ratio negative (-0.050) while the LLM signal outperforms it (Memmel p = 0.365)-consistent with genuine LLM-specific content, though the comparison itself is not statistically significant. We interpret the evidence as showing that LLM-extracted sentiment is highly sensitive to sampling variation, model choice, data source, and parameterization in ways a single point-estimate backtest cannot reveal, and propose this joint battery as a minimum robustness standard for future work.

detail.abstract: A number of new European Union (EU) law acts dealing with the digital economy reference fairness as one of their main goals or benchmarks, which has sparked renewed interest in the normative meaning of fairness and the role it plays in the regulation of the digital market. This paper draws on a private law theory of justice, that of commutative justice, to propose a reading of the term fairness within these acts and their new legal instruments, which is grounded in the principles of private law exchanges. Because access to and fair exchanges on digital markets lie at the heart of these acts, we develop a normative reconstruction of specific provisions of the acts that is based on an analysis of commutative justice and that provides a conceptual framework for interpreting and sharpening their objectives and instruments. In doing so, this paper wants to shed light on this central aspect of fairness and its implications for the emerging EU framework governing digital markets.

detail.abstract: With the flourishing development of social media, an all-new platform for the public opinion of leaders has appeared, and real-time feedback from the masses can now be shared here. This paper presents the Digital Narcissistic Reinforcement (DNR) loop, which is a self-perpetuating cycle of admiration-seeking behavior by narcissistic leaders, algorithmic reinforcement from platforms, and fan collective defense mechanisms; it strengthens the narcissistic leaders' grandiose self-concept and prevents corrective feedback. By combining research results from personality psychology, organizational behavior, communication studies, and computational social science, four themes have been proposed to support each of the three structural drivers in the loop: dispositional sensitivity to digital approval, structural privileging of grandiose content by algorithms, and fan identity fusion that purifies the leaders' information environment. The above studies have achieved some results in all fields and also found some shortcomings that need to be rectified. We identify four main research gaps and propose countermeasures for organizational governance, platform design and media literacy education. Theoretically consistent with reducing organizational risk under narcissistic leadership and empirically feasible, the DNR framework has been proposed.

detail.abstract: We introduce Euler centrality, an adjacency-based measure of structural indispensability in weighted social networks. Defined by the linear system (I + A)cE = 1, where A is the weighted adjacency matrix, this centrality quantifies each vertex's contribution to the network's effective size. Unlike degree, betweenness, or eigenvector centrality, Euler centrality captures structural uniqueness and yields positive, zero, or negative values, distinguishing indispensable brokers from redundant followers. In a case study on the weighted character network of Les Misérables, we show that Euler centrality identifies structurally essential characters overlooked by traditional metrics, offering a complementary perspective on substitutability, social influence, and network fragility.

detail.abstract:
A Brazilian DI rate move is routinely read as a shift in the market’s
Selic call, which is often wrong: it can instead reflect a change
in the compensation investors demand for Brazilian duration risk.
This paper separates the two using sixteen years of DI futures
data (2010–2026) and Adrian, Crump and Moench’s (2013) noarbitrage
framework, proposing term premium composition as a
marker for fiscal dominance risk versus credible policy delivery,
tested on two historical episodes and applied to 2025–26. Properly
controlling for US term premia means testing for cointegration,
not assuming it: both curves prove genuinely cointegrated
with their US counterparts, yielding a “basal” premium and a
direct measure of Brazil’s own share on top of it. The identical
machinery, applied to Brazil’s real (NTN-B) curve, recovers a real
term premium and breakeven decomposition against the same
control. A companion paper turns this machinery toward monetary

detail.abstract: The upcoming 6G technology promises significant advances in wireless communication, particularly in localization. This survey provides a comprehensive overview of state-of-the-art localization techniques for 6G, covering both terrestrial wireless approaches (e.g., WLAN and cellular) and space and aerial-based approaches (e.g., satellites and aircraft/HAPS). It discusses localization fundamentals, accuracy, and estimators for wireless networks, and examines the synergies between terrestrial networks (TNs) and non-terrestrial networks (NTNs). The paper also reviews platforms and architectures for NTN-based localization, enabling technologies for 6G NTNs, and representative use cases highlighting the potential benefits of non-terrestrial localization. Finally, it addresses key challenges and requirements for implementing high-accuracy localization in 6G and suggests future research directions.

title: Extractive Defaults: Asymmetrical Friction and the Interface Architecture of Financialized Attention

detail.title: Extractive Defaults: Asymmetrical Friction and the Interface Architecture of Financialized Attention

detail.abstract: Commercial platforms frequently introduce digital well-being features such as screen-time limits and break reminders that empirically fail to reduce usage. Unsealed litigation documents show these features are constrained by corporate guardrails engineered to prevent meaningful engagement loss. While dark patterns research catalogs manipulative UI tactics and critical political economy analyzes attention extraction, the mechanism translating macroeconomic pressure into software execution remains under-theorized. This article addresses this gap by introducing extractive defaults: a metrics-driven organizing logic that embeds financial-capitalist imperatives into software architecture. Under this logic, continuous attention capture functions as the non-negotiable baseline system state, forcing users to bear disproportionate cognitive and operational costs to opt out. Extractive defaults are operationalized through asymmetrical friction, systematically dissolving effort along pathways that extend session duration while compounding friction along pathways toward pause or exit. We trace how cross-site tracking, post-2008 financialization, and real-time bidding protocols established a per-second economic imperative to prolong engagement, which continuous experimentation pipelines translate directly into design. Analyzing three empirical modes-double extraction in paid tiers, manufactured scarcity and social obligation, and non-configurable interface closure-we demonstrate that current configurations historically displaced workable, user-centric alternatives. Finally, we propose three structural policy interventions: mandated choice symmetry, a right to a configurable interface, and system-level self-exclusion.

detail.abstract: High attrition disrupts business continuity and inflates hiring costs, and human-resource analytics increasingly promises to tell managers when an employee is nearing a breaking point. We test the widely asserted hypothesis that workload and commute distance compound multiplicatively to drive burnout and turnover, especially among Generation Z. Using five public HR datasets-849,999 synthetic employee records, three attrition cross-sections totalling 85,968 employees, and a 34,452 person-period panel-we find the hypothesis largely unsupported. The demand-by-distance interaction replicates in only one of three independent samples; random-effects pooling gives β 3 = 0.195 (p = 0.160) with I 2 = 94.6%. The Generation Z three-way term is null in all three samples (β 7 =-0.062, p = 0.098, I 2 = 0.0%). Lexicon-based sentiment analysis of 1,000 unique review documents recovers job demands-resources signals but no commute effect. We then formalise the managerial decision, deriving a value-adjusted intervention threshold p * i = C I /(τ κw i) and an expected-preventable-loss ranking. Out of sample, the conventional 0.5 cutoff forfeits up to 18.6 percentage points of attainable savings, whereas the model improves on a costs-only policy by less than one percentage point across 75% of the parameter space. Calibrating cost parameters dominates model accuracy.

detail.abstract: Operation-level trajectories are required upstream of ECAC Doc 29 aircraft-noise calculations, but crowdsourced ADS-B archives differ in terminal completeness. We present a source-adaptive workflow that converts OpenSky and ADS-B Exchange observations into runway-referenced trajectory products. OpenSky gaps near the runway are completed using runway geometry and AIP-derived approach references. ADS-B Exchange full traces are primarily extracted and trimmed while preserving observed runway roll. The retained 2025 result archive contains all 365 calendar days at both LEPA and LEMD. Of the conversion-manifest entries, 99.19–99.23% reached the B-2-oriented export. A 12-day cross-source comparison showed metre-scale observed lateral consistency and 99.3/98.0% conditional runway agreement. A separate 22-reference-day audit covered 550 airports in Spain, France and Portugal. Verified-completion airports represented 99.390% of Operations records and 99.370% of trace targets. The study stops at trajectory inputs. Acoustic propagation is outside scope.

detail.abstract: Distributional-regime methods often summarize market geometry with a small set of reference distributions. In the Distributional Regime Persistence (DRP) framework, the maintained representation has been a calm/stress pair of Wasserstein barycenters. This paper asks whether that two-anchor geometry is empirically sufficient. Using frozen pre-2007 calibration samples for the S&P 500, FTSE 100, Nikkei 225, and Hang Seng Index, I fit one-dimensional Wasserstein-1 k-medians representations with one to four prototypes and evaluate them strictly out of sample from January 2007 through June 2026. The analysis is repeated in raw return-distribution space and in independently median-centered, IQR-scaled shape space. Additional prototypes materially reduce out-of-sample reconstruction loss in every market and both spaces: moving from two to three prototypes lowers loss by 6.4%-9.6% in raw space and 7.9%-9.1% in shape space, while moving from three to four still lowers loss by 4.1%-6.4% and 2.8%-4.9%, respectively. Yet lower loss does not imply stable regime identity. Calibration-block bootstrap recurrence rejects several apparently useful extra prototypes, and the number of stable additional anchors differs by market and representation. Stable extra prototypes do, however, recur across markets under a frozen analogue criterion. The main result is therefore a dimensionality distinction: two anchors underfit distributional geometry, but approximation dimension exceeds stable identity dimension. Shape normalization does not eliminate the extra geometry, so the result cannot be reduced to finer volatility-scale partitioning.

detail.abstract: Whatever a language model's training reward rewards, the model learns to do. This paper charges the reward, by construction, for every response that breaks a written constitution: a finite set of enforceable clauses drawn from the law and from the codified ethics of the profession the model serves. Writing the penalised reward as the task reward minus a weight times the weighted clause violations, and solving the KL-regularised policy in closed form, we prove that compliance rises monotonically in the weight, that a computable threshold exists above which no violation is ever the reward-maximising response, that the cost of compliance is bounded by the weight times the violation removed, and that an imperfect detector opens a reward-hacking channel. A seeded simulation confirms each. Because compliance is a public good, an n-lab race makes defection dominant; a treaty with verification and a market-access sanction restores compliance once the expected sanction exceeds the largest private gain, and three to five of twelve jurisdictions suffice. The watchdog costs about what the IAEA costs, roughly $510 million a year, against tens of billions in avoided losses. Treaty articles, a watchdog protocol, and constitutions for an investment adviser and a clinic follow.

detail.abstract:
Where are the risks of a private equity manager actually observed, and why do supervisory, disclosure and due-diligence systems built around the manager fail to see them? Using 68 months of news-based incident data for Korea's largest buyout manager (20,637 risk articles and 6,208 incidents in the in-depth window to 30 August 2026; the five-manager benchmark window ends 26 July 2026, Table 1) and four domestic peers measured under identical rules, this paper documents a systematic mismatch between the unit at which risk occurs and the unit at which it is observed. Hypotheses and decision rules were fixed in a dated, hashed registration document (11 September 2026) before the results reported here were recomputed on the extended corpus; the public OSF registration of that document was filed on 13 September 2026, after the analyses, and is classed there as retrospective — a fact this paper does not conceal. The character of the registration differs by hypothesis: H5 and H6 were fixed before the underlying data were built, whereas H1 through H4 had observed values in prior outputs at the time their decision rules were fixed, as the registration itself states in Section 0 and as its amendment log records. Two of the six hypotheses were rejected under those rules, one was only partially supported, and one (H6) could not be estimated because its dependent-variable database was not completed; rejections, shortfalls and the unestimated hypothesis are reported in full. Classification validity was measured by a 400-item human double-coding: inter-coder kappa 0.80; against the human consensus, the production classifier reaches 0.61 and an independent second classifier 0.83; the verdicts are the same under both classifiers and under a filtering chain that uses no tone judgement.

Across all four non-listed managers, 90.8 to 96.2 percent of risk incidents are attributed to portfolio assets and only 3.8 to 9.2 percent to the manager entity. The single listed manager in the sample inverts this: 72.3 percent of its incidents attach to the entity, roughly eleven times the non-listed level, and the contrast survives a change of classification tool (9.4 times). Entity-level signal is therefore low not because risk is absent but because no observation window exists. Risk is also extremely concentrated: two assets account for 84.4 percent of incidents, and 2.71 percent of incidents capture 37.3 percent of all coverage.

Did the crisis then spread across the portfolio? Under a pre-registered difference-in-differences design the answer is no. The treatment effect on exposure-adjusted incident density is 0.42 (95% CI -1.77 to 2.61); in a matched subsample where the parallel-trends assumption holds it is -0.51 (-2.12 to 1.10). Ten placebo and robustness specifications produce no exception. Averages, however, conceal heterogeneity. A descriptive transmission map shows that what moved was not incidents but names: on exposure-adjusted density, own-asset incidents at other holdings fell for 14 of 17 risk types, though in raw counts they were essentially unchanged at 1,038 against 1,035, with most of the decline coming from a single asset; meanwhile articles linking those assets to the failing one rose five- to twenty-fold, the phrase "the next Homeplus" went from zero to 37 articles, and the share of articles naming the manager that also mention the failing asset rose from 2.3 to 67.1 percent. Transmission ran from asset to the manager's name, not from asset to asset.

H6, on the determinants of the public response, could not be estimated: its registered dependent variable — public-authority actions coded by date from primary sources — was built within this study only for 29 records from December 2024 onward, so the channel-by-month panel from 2021 does not exist. Every source is public, and the registered design can be estimated as specified once the database is completed.

publicationDetails.detailsText: Journal of Risk and Uncertainty, Forthcoming

detail.abstract: Embedded in the value of a statistical life (VSL) is a stream of valuations of each expected year of life. The value of a statistical life year (VSLY) has a policy-relevant role analogous to the VSL, except that it monetizes risks to short periods of life extension. This article reviews previous studies and reports new labor market estimates of the average VSLY and the variation of these values with age using two methods-inferring the average VSLY based on estimates of the VSL and a new method that provides direct empirical estimates of the valuation of a discounted life year. The direct estimates of the VSLY yield larger values than the constructed estimates. The VSLY based on fatality rates by industry and occupation is $600,000 to $800,000 at a 3 percent interest rate. Estimates based on age-adjusted fatality rates are somewhat lower. The discount rate used in assessing the VSLY has a pivotal effect on the estimated VSLY. The VSLY is substantially lower in the absence of discounting and more than doubled at a discount rate of 10 percent. Failure to use a positive discount rate greatly understates the VSLY. The article also reviews previous VSLY studies as well as estimates of the discount rate for years of life expectancy.

title: What a Difference Useful Exergy Makes: Energy Boundaries and the Magnitude of Economy-Wide Rebound

detail.title: What a Difference Useful Exergy Makes: Energy Boundaries and the Magnitude of Economy-Wide Rebound

detail.abstract: This study demonstrates that estimates of the economy-wide rebound effect depend on how energy is measured and where the analytical boundary is drawn along the energy-conversion chain. Estimating two normalized Constant Elasticity of Substitution (CES) production functions for Portugal over the period 1960-2014, the study provides a consistent local comparative-static analysis of rebound effects on the aggregate supply-side based on two energy measures: final energy and useful exergy. Useful exergy extends the analytical boundary beyond the conventional final energy consumption to capture, in a thermodynamically consistent manner, the energy delivered as a service. Accounting for both substitution and output effects, the results indicate a partial economy-wide rebound of 48.8% at the final energy boundary. At the useful exergy boundary, the estimated rebound rises to 106.3%, indicating slight backfire: efficiency-induced savings in useful exergy are fully offset, and useful exergy demand increases. Bootstrap estimates confirm the robustness of this result. These findings are consistent with the stylized facts of declining final energy intensity but a comparatively stable relationship between economic output and useful exergy input. The analysis highlights the need for rebound studies to be explicit in their energy measure and analytical boundary. It also challenges the assumption that efficiency improvements necessarily reduce the economy-wide demand for physical energy services. The persistence of this demand suggests that future decoupling between economic growth and energy services may be more difficult to achieve than commonly assumed.

title: Navier-Stokes Computation for the Growth of a Vapor Bubble Nucleating from a Surface

detail.title: Navier-Stokes Computation for the Growth of a Vapor Bubble Nucleating from a Surface

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author is the brother of S. Madhavan, whose 1969 PhD dissertation is the principal historical artifact examined in this paper. S. Madhavan reviewed the manuscript for accuracy concerning the 1969 research. No financial conflict of interest is reported.

keywords: history of scientific computing JEL Classification: O33

detail.abstract: In 1969, S. Madhavan used an axisymmetric free-boundary Navier-Stokes calculation to predict the evolving shape of vapor bubbles growing on an unheated surface in an isothermal, bulk-superheated liquid. The experiment and computation were deliberately simplified together: rapid depressurization created a nearly uniform superheat without a heated-wall thermal boundary layer, while the computation supplied the measured volume history through an automated pressure-feedback loop rather than solving the temperature field and phase-change kinetics. From a photographed initial profile and a fixed footprint, the subsequent nonspherical shape evolution was computed with an adapted Marker-and-Cell method, a problem-specific split-spline interface representation, curvature-dependent surface tension, and pressure iteration on a mesh of roughly 600 cells. Calculated profiles were compared graphically with 5,000-frame/s photographs. The same program was used to isolate detachment forces, while the experimental program produced rapid-depressurization and microlayer-related findings that later entered distinct research lines. This paper reconstructs Madhavan's 1969 computational advancement, then follows how its findings were used, tested, and reinterpreted, and how the computational scope was independently extended from the 1970s through the 2020s. NASA-sponsored boiling-transient research used the Madhavan-Mesler no-delay observation to frame and reconcile conflicting nucleation evidence; Malcotsis later provided independent experimental support for bubble detachment without buoyancy; later boiling CFD added the temperature field, complete-cycle treatment, general interface methods, microlayer physics, conjugate heat transfer, and three-dimensional computation. The resulting history is one of technical knowledge traveling farther than the original artifact. Later specialist literature identifies the associated 1970 work, with explicit qualification, as an early or first-known MAC-based boiling simulation; the present paper treats that as a qualified historical placement rather than an absolute worldwide-priority claim. The paper therefore treats formulation, rather than computing power alone, as the enabling resource of the 1969 work.

detail.abstract: Fast loan growth predicts subsequent losses at banks, but the channel through which lenders grow is unobservable in regulatory data. This paper exploits a feature of U.S. credit union call reports that separates loans originated through third-party dealers from loans originated directly with members and carries a dedicated charge-off series for the dealer-originated book. Using 46,618 credit-union-quarters from 2014 to 2026, an expansion of dealer-originated auto lending equal to one standard deviation of the vehicle portfolio is followed by a 2.6 to 2.8 basis point increase in annualized net charge-offs concentrated five to twelve quarters after origination, with no effect in the first year and a fading effect by the fourth, matching the seasoning profile of auto credit. Direct and dealer-originated growth generate statistically indistinguishable losses: the risk lies in the pace of expansion, not the channel. The channels differ only on cost, with dealer-originated growth lowering return on assets in the first two years. Loan yields do not rise after either form of growth, so the additional risk was not priced. A second design exploits the 2021 used-vehicle price surge as a shock to institutions whose reliance on dealers was fixed before it: a one-standard-deviation higher pre-pandemic indirect share is followed by 4 to 6 basis points more seasoned loss after the surge, with no differential trend before it. The results extend the loan-growth literature to a cooperative lender type and a quarterly horizon, and speak to a documented gap in public data on nonbank auto finance.

detail.title: Convenience Matters: Nudging Patients Toward Telemedicine

declarations.declarationOfInterest: No interest

detail.abstract: Healthcare providers increasingly operate telemedicine alongside in-person services, yet patients often default to in-person appointments, limiting effective capacity utilization across channels. Providers can influence channel choice through system-level controls such as pricing, capacity allocation, and channel availability, but these interventions can be costly, slow, or restricted by regulation. We investigate whether low-cost, rapidly deployable informational interventions can shift patient channel choice, particularly during infectious disease outbreaks when demand management is most valuable. We develop two informational interventions: an infection message that highlights the infection risks associated with in-person care (or their elimination through telemedicine) and a convenience message that emphasizes the ease of self-scheduling telemedicine appointments, enabling earlier access to care. We evaluate these interventions through a series of online experiments and estimate a structural random utility model to identify the behavioral mechanisms underlying channel choice. We find that when channels already differ in price or appointment wait time due to system-level controls, informational messages have little additional effect. When channels are otherwise equivalent, both message types can significantly increase telemedicine uptake. The convenience message consistently increases telemedicine uptake across participants from different countries and diverse demographic backgrounds. The infection message is effective in studies that coincide with ongoing communicable disease outbreaks. The structural model confirms that both infection fear and attitude toward wait time are meaningful drivers of channel choice. Healthcare providers can use targeted, low-cost informational messaging as a practical demand management tool to shift patients toward telemedicine. Convenience messaging, in particular, is a broadly applicable method for encouraging telemedicine adoption, both during and beyond infectious disease outbreaks.

detail.abstract: We measure two dimensions of politics in college courses-the amount of political content and its partisan orientation-using course descriptions from nearly 1,000 U.S. colleges and universities over the past 25 years. Using a novel text-as-data method, we separate the amount of "political content," the extent to which a course engages with topics salient to politics and public policy, from "slant," the partisan direction of that content. Since 2000, the average course has 0.15 SD more political content and 0.13 SD more liberal slant. Changes are most pronounced in the tails of the distribution, particularly for slant, and are modest relative to persistent cross-field differences. Following instructors who move between institutions, we find that instructors account for 60-65% of cross-sectional differences in course political content and slant. Using enrollment data, we find students show no preference for liberal content before the 2010s; demand for liberal content rises over the following decade, peaks in 2020, and falls slightly thereafter.

detail.abstract: E-cigarettes and nicotine pouches have become increasingly prominent in European markets, yet their rapid product innovation and compositional heterogeneity have exposed important limitations in existing excise tax frameworks. This paper analyzes how EU27 Member States have approached the taxation of these products, documenting a strong convergence toward simple excise systems based on observable physical quantities, primarily volume for e-liquids and weight for nicotine pouches, alongside a small number of departures based on nicotine concentration. Drawing on comparative policy analysis, country case studies, and a targeted review of the health economics literature, the paper evaluates whether these alternative tax bases meaningfully improve alignment between taxation and health risk. The analysis finds that nicotine concentration performs poorly as a proxy for harm in both the e-cigarette and nicotine pouch context and introduces complexity that exceeds the enforcement capacity of most excise administrations. Attention is given to the interaction between tax design and the broader enforcement environment in which alternative products operate. These market characteristics complicate product oversight and weaken the ability of tax authorities to verify product characteristics, particularly in fragmented and import-dependent supply chains. This paper argues that excise taxation cannot, on its own, resolve broader regulatory challenges related to product standards, market surveillance, and enforcement. Accordingly, effective tax design requires a clear delineation between what excise systems can achieve and what must be addressed through complementary regulatory instruments. Overloading excise structures with corrective objectives risks weakening both their fiscal and policy effectiveness. This study therefore points to a set of practical design principles centered on administrable, volume and weight-based excise structures, complemented by non-tax regulatory measures, as the most robust approach for governing nicotine markets.

detail.abstract: Roughly a third of the food produced worldwide is wasted, with retail accounting for a substantial share of this loss. Surplus-food platforms such as Too Good To Go (TGTG) address this challenge by partnering with retailers, allowing them to sell discounted "surprise bags" of near-expiry food items via a mobile app. We combine two years of data from 5,279 U.S. convenience stores of the global chain Circle K with store-level TGTG data to provide the first large-scale causal evaluation of such a partnership. Exploiting staggered platform adoption in a difference-indifferences design, we find that TGTG adoption reduces fresh and prepared-food waste by around 11% while increasing store traffic and revenue by 5%, with no significant change in average basket value, indicating that the platform generates incremental store visits rather than cannibalizing existing demand. The partnership creates value through operational and demand channels, which evolve on distinct timescales: waste reduction is immediate and largely persistent, while demand grows gradually as consumers discover the platform. Category-level analyses reveal positive spillovers into non-food categories alongside substitution in products that overlap with surprise bag contents, and higher consumer ratings are associated with stronger engagement during a store's early months on the platform. Our findings show that surplus-food platforms can simultaneously provide environmental and commercial benefits: during our study, the partnership amounts to 2.5M units of reduced waste and additional revenue of $218.3M.

detail.abstract:
This paper presents a formal macroeconomic mechanism design to resolve sovereign debt compounding under $r > g$ and dismantle the modern Triffin Dilemma. The framework establishes a Bifurcated Sovereign Monetary Standard that decouples international trade settlement velocity from the balance-sheet solvency of the reserve issuer. At the transactional layer, legacy correspondent networks (SWIFT) and unbacked Eurodollars are supplanted by programmable USD stablecoins collateralized 1:1 by ultra-short Treasury bills (T-Bills). This ensures atomic trade settlement ($\tau \to 0$) while continuously absorbing short-duration fiscal deficits without domestic inflation.

At the reserve layer, long-term public debt is restructured into Collateralized Sovereign Bonds (CSBs) across 10- to 30-year maturities, backed by an Algorithmic Dual-Asset Sovereign Sinking Fund (AD-SF) maintaining a 50/50 reserve of vaulted gold and sovereign Bitcoin. To overcome compressed cash coupons (1.25%–2.75%), CSBs embed an institutional participation kicker granting investors a contractual 15%–25% share of terminal asset surplus—evaluated via a manipulation-resistant 90-day VWAP—while 75%–85% of surplus capital permanently extinguishes sovereign debt.

Through double-entry accounting proofs, institutional game theory (Nash equilibrium), and stress-testing, we show that:

  • Initial capitalization avoids spot price shocks via statutory gold certificate revaluations and in-kind debt swaps;

  • Algorithmic rebalancing operates via seigniorage yields rather than forced sales; and

  • Expropriation risks under the Lucas Critique are neutralized via a domestic bankruptcy-remote Statutory SPV, on-chain Proof of Reserves, and statutory cross-default covenants.

A $1 trillion, 10-year sovereign simulation confirms that an actuarially conservative 5.24% CAGR fully amortizes nominal debt liabilities while generating over $4.4 trillion in unencumbered sovereign net equity.

detail.abstract: On October 1, 2026, the United States begins mandatory implementation of the ICH E2B(R3) standard for post-market individual case safety reports. The standard captures patient demographics, concomitant medications, and laboratory values, but not housing stability, food security, or healthcare access. This commentary argues that the U.S. pharmacovigilance system is structurally incapable of distinguishing pharmacological risk from social vulnerability, leading to two complementary errors: missed harm and false certainty about subgroup effects. Drawing on the JAMA Health Forum audit finding that 57.5% of Sentinel's safety concerns were unassessable, the FDA's own acknowledgment of "insufficient capture of race and ethnicity," and the unresolved ALLHAT signal on ACE inhibitors in Black patients, the piece proposes four structural reforms for the PDUFA VIII reauthorization: prospective subgroup surveillance with prespecified analyses; routine causal calibration using E-values; expansion of the surveillance network's social-contextual depth, including a supplementary domestic reporting standard; and evidentiary reversal criteria with sunset provisions. The piece is a policy commentary, not a research article.

title: AI and the Public Accessibility Principle: Rethinking Prior Art in the Age of Data-Centered Inventions

detail.title: AI and the Public Accessibility Principle: Rethinking Prior Art in the Age of Data-Centered Inventions

declarations.declarationOfInterest: No relationship to any people or organization relevant to the topic
declarations.funderStatement: None

detail.abstract:
This Article argues that artificial intelligence (AI) and other data-centered inventions expose a fundamental weakness in traditional patent novelty doctrine: commercialization no longer reliably makes an invention publicly accessible. Historically, patent systems treated public use and sale as proxies for accessibility because inventions were embodied in products that could be observed, analyzed, or reverse engineered. AI systems, by contrast, often disclose functionality while concealing the inventive contribution, including training data, model architectures, learned parameters, and data-processing methods
Through a comparative analysis of the European Patent Convention (EPC) and U.S. patent law, the Article contends that public accessibility should be the sole foundation for determining prior art and novelty. It shows that the EPC’s accessibility-based approach is better suited to AI than U.S. doctrines that treat secret commercial exploitation as novelty-destroying prior art and permit anticipation through inherency without public access to the relevant information. The Article further argues that the America Invents Act’s transition to a first-inventor-to-file system undermines the justification for doctrines such as Helsinn, Metallizing Engineering, and experimental use.
To address the challenges posed by AI, the Article proposes an overarching public-accessibility standard under which hidden features of AI systems constitute prior art only when a person skilled in the art could identify them through lawfully available information and ordinary technical efforts. Such a standard would improve legal certainty, promote international harmonization, and better align novelty doctrine with the technological realities of the AI era.

title: CLEAR™: From Classical Rhetoric to a Modern Marketing Communication Framework

detail.title: CLEAR™: From Classical Rhetoric to a Modern Marketing Communication Framework

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author is President and Chief Architect of OPEX Institute Inc., which holds a commercial interest in the CLEAR™ framework described in this paper. No data collection, funding, or third-party commercial arrangements are currently associated with this working paper.

detail.abstract:
Marketing communication has never suffered from a shortage of persuasion techniques. Classical rhetoric gave us ethos, logos, pathos, and kairos. Modern research has added source credibility, dual-process models of persuasion, narrative transportation, consumer relevance, persuasion knowledge, trust, and involvement. Yet a practical problem remains. A message can be credible but irrelevant, logical but emotionally disconnected. It can show real empathy and still land at the wrong moment — timely, yet wrong for the situation. And personalization on its own, a name inserted where a name fits, does not guarantee that anyone cares.

This paper proposes CLEAR, an integrative framework organized around five receiver-centered questions: Credibility (Can I believe you?), Logic (Does this make sense?), Empathy (Do you understand me?), Alignment (Does this fit my situation?), and Relevance (Why should I care?). Each dimension is grounded in an established research tradition — source credibility theory, the Elaboration Likelihood Model, narrative transportation research, kairos-based rhetorical theory, and perceived relevance research, respectively — and the paper's contribution is integrative rather than substitutive.

CLEAR is explicitly proposed as a research framework, not a validated theory. The paper specifies thirteen testable hypotheses, a proposed structural model (CLEAR dimensions → Consumer Trust → Purchase Intention, with direct and moderated paths), five competing measurement models for empirical comparison, and a three-study research program (scale development, predictive modeling, experimental validation). No data has been collected; all claims are pre-registration-stage propositions. The central research question — whether the five dimensions can be operationalized as distinct but related constructs that explain variance beyond established models — is designed to permit failure, and the framework will be revised or abandoned if discriminant, predictive, or incremental validity is not demonstrated.

This working draft (v0.7) is intended to invite critical feedback from marketing, communication, and consumer psychology researchers ahead of Study 1 data collection.
